children.text: yasminn udayati vikasati kamalam ivāstaṃ prayāti saṃkucati/
children.translated_text: At whose rising the lotus blooms, and at whose setting it closes —

children.text: sacarācaraṃ tribhuvanaṃ sa jayati kiraṇālayaḥ savitā//
children.translated_text: that <s>Savitā</s> (the Sun), abode of rays, conquers the three worlds with all that moves and does not move.

children.text: yakṣeśamedhena vijitya dhātrīm ity evam abhyudyamino nṛpasya/
children.translated_text: Having conquered the earth by means of a sacrifice to <s>Yakṣeśa</s> (Lord of the <s>Yakṣas</s>) — thus for a king who is striving,

children.text: vinighnato vighnakarān na pāpaṃ kriyāt krameṇaiva paśūn makheṣu//
children.translated_text: who destroys those who cause obstacles — there is no sin in [sacrificing] animals at sacrifices in due order.
Endowed with vigor, counsel, lordly power, and strength; wise, with subdued senses and a disciplined retinue;

children.text: prajānurakto dhṛtimān sahiṣṇur vṛddhopasevī vijigīṣur iṣṭaḥ//
children.translated_text: beloved of his subjects, steadfast, forbearing, devoted to the company of elders — such is the desirable conqueror.

children.text: sāmvatsaras tasya vinītaveṣo dhīmān svatantrāṅgapaṭuḥ kulīnaḥ/
children.translated_text: His <s>sāṃvatsara</s> (royal astrologer) should be of modest appearance, wise, skilled in the independent limbs [of astrology], of noble birth,

children.text: dakṣaḥ pragalbho 'vikalo vinītas tādṛg vidhastasya purohito 'pi//
children.translated_text: capable, bold, free from deficiencies, and disciplined — such also should be his <s>purohita</s> (royal chaplain).
The learned describe the attainment of results as dependent on both fate and human effort;

children.text: tatra kecid avadhūya nṛkāraṃ daivam eva phaladāyakam āhuḥ//
children.translated_text: among them, some, dismissing human effort, declare fate alone to be the giver of results.

children.text: labdhavyāny eva labhyate gantavyāny eva gacchati/
children.translated_text: What is to be obtained is indeed obtained, what is to be gone to is indeed gone to;

children.text: prāptavyāny eva prāproti duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca//
children.translated_text: what is to be reached is indeed reached — both sufferings and pleasures.

children.text: utthānāc ced bhavet siddhir na kaścit prāpnuyāt phalam/
children.translated_text: If success came from effort alone, no one would ever attain a [bad] result;
[yet] those who toil day and night are seen emaciated by [the struggle for] livelihood.
Like a bird indeed, death may fall [upon one]; <s>Aryaman</s> is lord [of fate],
appointed by destiny, invisible to others — he is master neither of others nor of himself.

children.text: tasmād daivaṃ pradhānaṃ hi na kuryāt karma mānuṣam/
children.translated_text: Therefore fate is supreme — one should not perform human action;

children.text: niśceṣṭam api loke 'smin bhajate bhuktir uttamā//
children.translated_text: even without effort in this world, the highest enjoyment comes to one.

children.text: āghātadurjayanayaṃ paribhūya daivam ātmābhimānacapalāḥ pracaranti ye 'rīn/
children.translated_text: Those who, arrogantly scorning fate — which is difficult to defeat by assault and stratagem — rush against enemies,

children.text: teṣāṃ cirād api kṛtāntamahāpaśūnāṃ hastagrahaṃ na samupaiti jitāpi lakṣmī//
children.translated_text: for them, even after a long time, prosperity once won does not return to grasp their hand, [for they are] great sacrificial victims of <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death).
Likewise, others, without regard for fate, relying on courage,
looking only to the success of action, have proclaimed effort alone.

children.text: utthānahīno rājā hi buddhimān api sarvadā/
children.translated_text: A king devoid of effort, though wise in every way,
is assailable by enemies, like a serpent without venom.
A man resolute in effort stands above those resolute only in speech;
those resolute in speech attend upon and delight the one resolute in effort.
One who is dull in calculating destiny and drowsy in regard for human effort
does not kiss the face of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) despite the exertions of wishful thinking.
For those whose sole conviction is decided by valor — immediately upon hearing [the call],
the lion-like [warrior], fragrant with rut, drinks the sweet tear-nectar of the elephant.
The fruitions of results are seen to follow plowing and rain together;
on this matter, hear the verses uttered from the mouth of <s>Dvāpāyana</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>):

children.text: na vinā mānuṣaṃ daivaṃ daivaṃ vā mānuṣaṃ vinā/
children.translated_text: Neither fate without human effort, nor human effort without fate,
can by itself accomplish an objective — just as a single fire-stick cannot [produce] fire.
All undertakings succeed from the conjunction of action and prosperity,

children.text: daivāt purusakārāc ca na tv ekasmāt kathājcana//
children.translated_text: from fate and human effort combined — never from one alone.
Fate instructs a man: 'Be here!' — as the instructor;
'I shall not be here for him' — whence then is fruit without aspiration?

children.text: yatnena sampadya manuṣyakāraṃ yatnāvakāśe puruṣo niruddhaḥ/
children.translated_text: Having accomplished human effort with exertion, a man who is blocked in the scope of effort

children.text: pratīkṣate daivamataṃ dvitīyas tam āpado nātmakṛtāḥ spṛśanti//
children.translated_text: then awaits the verdict of fate — such a one is not touched by self-caused misfortunes.
The fruit of <s>karma</s> earned by one's nature is easily ripened by the enterprise of a king;

children.text: kṛcchreṇa śeṣaṃ mahatā yato 'to bhājyāni mṛgyāṇi nṛbhir nṛkāraiḥ//E20
children.translated_text: the remainder [is accomplished] with great difficulty — therefore what is to be enjoyed must be sought by men through human effort.
Chapter 2: Qualities of the <s>Tithi</s> (Lunar Day)

children.text: yātrākālam ataḥ paraṃ munimatāny ālokya saṃkhyāpayā-
children.translated_text: Henceforth I shall enumerate the time for military expedition, having examined the doctrines of the sages,
having set forth in detail what has been accomplished regarding the weighty syllables, addressing the Lord of the Earth.

children.text: jñāte janmani tasya yānasamayaṃ vāṃchanti horāvidas
children.translated_text: When the birth [horoscope] is known, the experts in <s>horā</s> (horoscopy) desire the time of the journey,

children.text: tv ajñāte 'py aphaleṣu nākṣaram iva prāhātra ratnāvalim//
children.translated_text: but even when it is unknown, for fruitless [cases], they have declared here the 'String of Jewels' — as though not [even] a syllable [is wasted].
When the <s>horā</s>-sign is known, and the position and strength of the planets are grasped,

children.text: āyuṣi ca parijñāte śubham aśubhaṃ vā phalaṃ vācyam//
children.translated_text: and the lifespan has been ascertained, the auspicious or inauspicious result should be declared.
Others say that even when the birth-time is unknown,
a suitable time for departure can be [determined] for kings;
the great <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s> has spoken this word, endowed with the fruits arising from
the ascendant of questions, attaining success and fortune in the truth of things.

children.text: apṛcchataḥ pṛcchato vā yiyāsor yasya kasya cit/
children.translated_text: Whether one asks or does not ask, for anyone who wishes to depart,
one should determine the auspicious or inauspicious from the <s>horā</s>, the <s>kendra</s> (angular houses), and the <s>trikoṇa</s> (trines).
For the astrologer, by fate, whether desiring good or bad results,
every mortal is involuntarily brought within his range of observation.

children.text: aśrauṣīc ca purā viṣṇor jñānārthaṃ samupasthitaḥ/
children.translated_text: And he formerly heard, having approached for the sake of knowledge,
the words of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of the World, issued from his lotus-mouth:

children.text: yat sāraṃ pṛcchataḥ puṃso graharā(śyā)śritaṃ phalam/
children.translated_text: Whatever is the essence of the planetary and sign-based result for the person who asks,

children.text: tatsāraṃ tasya janma syād ya(dya)py anyagṛhe bhavet//
children.translated_text: that essence becomes his nativity, even if it were in another's house.
Having understood the <s>śāstra</s> (science) properly, according to the determination of strengths and weaknesses,
one should consider everything here just as stated for the birth-chart.
Therefore the king, with flowers, jewels, and fruits in his hands,
in the morning, having bowed to the Sun, facing the eastern direction,
having assembled astrologers skilled in the limbs of <s>horā</s>-science and who are beneficent,
should consult the astronomical calculators all at once.
Then, when the astrologer is merely asked in the king's presence,
he should infer the result from the omens of exertion, with the vision of the <s>śāstra</s>.

children.text: sad iti sadasi vācyaṃ yady api syād asat tat
children.translated_text: What is good should be declared as good in the assembly, even if it were actually bad —

children.text: sphuṭam pai kathanīyaṃ bhūbhuje mantriṇe vā//
children.translated_text: clearly, [the result] should be told to the king or to the minister.
On ground covered with trees bearing sweet fruits, flowers, and milky sap,
where walking is pleasant, where there is cow-dung, drinkable [water],
with water and flowers, after bathing — facing upward auspiciously,
one who knows the movements of planets and stars should pronounce [the result] to the questioner.
If the king touches with his fingertips his breast, soles of the feet, lips, thumb, hand, or upper limbs,
or ears, face, nose, private parts, or orifices,
or cheek, hip, or shoulder —
if he speaks an auspicious word, the army will subdue the enemies.

children.text: udayam udayapaṃ vā janmabhaṃ janmapaṃ vā
children.translated_text: Having examined the ascendant or ascendant-lord, or the birth-sign or birth-lord,

children.text: tad upacayagṛhaṃ vā vīkṣya lagne yiyāsoḥ/
children.translated_text: or the house of its growth, in the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant) of the one wishing to depart —

children.text: vinihatam aripakṣaṃ viddhi śatror idaṃ vā
children.translated_text: know that the enemy's side is defeated; or this is the enemy's [result],
if it is conjoined with the fourth house of the questioner, or placed in the seventh.

children.text: pārṣṇigrāhaḥ pṛṣṭhato bhāskarasya prāg yātavyastigmaraśmeś ca yānaḥ/
children.translated_text: The rear guard is behind the Sun; the march is in the direction ahead of the sharp-rayed one;

children.text: ākrandārkāt saptame yaḥ sthitaś ca tattulyāste śaktitaś cintayīyāḥ//
children.translated_text: the one who stands in the seventh from the <s>ākranda</s> (alarm-cry) [house reckoned] from the Sun — those of equal [rank] should be considered according to their strength.
When <s>Jīva</s> (Jupiter), <s>Jña</s> (Mercury), the Sun, and <s>Sita</s> (Venus) occupy the 5th, 4th, bad, <s>lagna</s>, and 11th houses,

children.text: siddhārtho 'rigaṇān vijitya na cirāt praṣṭā sametyālayam/
children.translated_text: the questioner, having conquered the enemy host, soon returns home with his objective accomplished.

children.text: lagne vā kujamandayoḥ sutagate jīve ravau karmage
children.translated_text: When Mars and Saturn are in the <s>lagna</s>, Jupiter in the 5th, the Sun in the 10th,

children.text: lābhe karmaṇi vā sitendusutayoḥ praṣṭur jayo niścitaḥ//
children.translated_text: and Venus and Mercury's son (Mercury) are in the 11th or 10th — the questioner's victory is certain.

children.text: tasminn eva bhaved yoge yadi śukro 'ṣṭam āśritaḥ/
children.translated_text: In that very combination, if <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) occupies the 8th,

children.text: praṣṭāram udyamād eva hataśaktir viśasty ariḥ//
children.translated_text: the enemy, [though] with depleted strength, destroys the questioner through sheer exertion.
Success [comes] when <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), the Sun, and the Moon are placed in the <s>lagna</s>, 6th, or 10th;
likewise when Jupiter, Venus, and the Sun are in the <s>lagna</s>, 6th, or 8th.
The acquisition of a minister [comes] when <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) is in the 11th, Saturn and Mars in the 10th;

children.text: caturthe jñe 'ṣṭame candre jāyāsthe ca site jayaḥ//
children.translated_text: with Mercury in the 4th, the Moon in the 8th, and Venus in the 7th — victory.
When Mars is in the 10th, the Sun in the 11th, Saturn in the 3rd,

children.text: candre ṣaṣṭhe vilagnasthaiḥ śeṣaiḥ praṣṭurdhruvo jayaḥ//
children.translated_text: the Moon in the 6th, and the remaining [planets] in the <s>lagna</s> — the questioner's victory is certain.
Victory with the Sun, Saturn, and Mars in the 3rd, and the benefics in the <s>lagna</s>;

children.text: gurau vā lagnage pāpair lābhe karmaṇi vā sthitaiḥ//
children.translated_text: or when <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) is in the <s>lagna</s>, with malefics in the 11th or 10th.
When Mars and Saturn are in the 6th, Jupiter and the Moon in the <s>lagna</s>,
Venus and Mercury at the end [of a sign], the sharp-rayed one (Mars) in the 10th — victory.

children.text: ity yogāḥ śubhāḥ proktāḥ praśnakāle jayāśritāḥ/
children.translated_text: Thus the auspicious combinations have been declared, related to victory at the time of the question;

children.text: aśubhās tu bhavanty atra tān pravakṣyāmy ataḥ param//
children.translated_text: but inauspicious ones also occur here — I shall declare those hereafter.
Defeat in battle when Saturn, the Moon, and Mars are in the 9th, 1st, and <s>lagna</s>;
death when the Moon and Saturn are in the <s>lagna</s>, aspected by Mars.

children.text: savakre nidhane mande mṛtyur lagne divākare/
children.translated_text: Death when retrograde Saturn is in the 8th; when the Sun is in the <s>lagna</s>,

children.text: candre 'smin tryāyamṛtyusthe sasūrye vā vaded vadham//
children.translated_text: with the Moon in the 3rd, 11th, or 8th with the death-lord [placed there], or with the Sun — one should predict slaughter.
Destruction of the questioner even as he goes, when retrograde Mercury and the Moon are in the 10th;
increase of famine, death, and enemies when Mars and Venus are in the <s>lagna</s>.
When the Moon and Mars are in the 1st, Mercury and Venus in the 6th,
and the Sun in the 8th — the death of the minister should be predicted.
The death of the questioner's son when malefics are in the ascendant and 5th;
defeat when the Moon conjoins Mars in the <s>lagna</s>, aspected by Saturn.
When the Moon is in the 10th and 8th, the Sun in the <s>lagna</s>,
or in the reverse — for one who has gone, the approach of fear, defeat, and death.
When malefics are placed in the 2nd, 3rd, and angular houses, and benefics are devoid of strength,
and the Moon is in the 8th — the questioner [faces] imprisonment, death, and calamity.
Dissension in one's own [camp] when Mars and the Moon are in the 10th, the Sun and Mercury in the ascendant;

children.text: tadvan mandārayor yuddhe bhaṅgaḥ saumyārkayos tathā//
children.translated_text: likewise defeat in battle when Saturn and Mars, or Mercury and the Sun [are in similar positions].

children.text: sarvais tu navame rājā hanti mantripurohitān/
children.translated_text: When all [malefics] are in the 9th, the king slays his ministers and chaplains;
in this combination, with the Moon in the ascendant, [he slays] the son, the architect, and the teachers.
When the Sun and Saturn are in the <s>lagna</s>, aspected by Mars,

children.text: candre 'ste vibalaiḥ saumyaiḥ praṣṭuḥ senāpater vadhaḥ//
children.translated_text: with the Moon in the 7th and weak benefics — the death of the questioner's general.
When retrograde Saturn is in the 8th, the Moon in the 7th, the Sun in the <s>lagna</s>,

children.text: jñe tṛtīye ca vikramya samantrī hanyate nṛpaḥ//
children.translated_text: and Mercury in the 3rd — having attacked, the king is slain together with his minister.
When the ascendant is aspected by or conjoined with benefic friends,
and the <s>lagna</s> has powerful benefics in the benefic divisions of the <s>lagna</s>,
it is productive of success; the undesired [result occurs] when otherwise than this —
other [considerations for] enterprise are determined by the methods of birth and journey results.
Malefics in the 8th, 4th, <s>horā</s>, 7th, and 2nd houses
do not produce auspicious results for human questioners;
benefics are praised when conjoined with the 10th house among these;
all this, good and bad without exception, should also be considered at the time of the journey.
Chapter 3: Qualities of the <s>Tithi</s> (Lunar Day)

children.text: nandā bhadrā vijayāś cātha riktāḥ pūrṇāś caitāḥ phalam evaṃ vidadhyuḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Nandā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, then <s>Riktā</s>, and <s>Pūrṇā</s> — these produce results thus:

children.text: neṣṭā madhyā pravarāś ceti śukle kṛṇṇe cintyās tithayas tāḥ pratīpāḥ//
children.translated_text: undesired, middling, and excellent in the bright fortnight; in the dark fortnight, those <s>tithis</s> are to be considered in reverse.

children.text: sarvāḥ śastās tithayaḥ śuklapakṣe hitvā tryṃśaṃ bahule 'ntyaṃ ca kaiścit/
children.translated_text: All <s>tithis</s> in the bright fortnight are auspicious except the 30th; some [say] also the last in the dark fortnight;

children.text: ṣaṣṭhyaṣṭamyor vasulabdhāpi yātā dvādaśyāṃ vā nāśam āśu prayāti//
children.translated_text: one who departs on the 6th or 8th even if having obtained wealth, or on the 12th, quickly goes to destruction.

children.text: pratipadi phalam eke pañcadaśyāṃ ca neṣṭaṃ jagur idam iti tajjñair yāpyam evāvadhāryam/
children.translated_text: Some have said that the result on the 1st and the 15th is undesired — this should be understood as acceptable by the experts;

children.text: kim api kim api nūnaṃ taiḥ samīkṣyoktam etat samavacanavighāte yuktatā kena cintyā//E3
children.translated_text: surely something has been said by them after careful consideration — when there is contradiction among equal authorities, who can judge the propriety?
Chapter 4: Strength of the <s>Nakṣatra</s> (Lunar Mansion)
In each direction, groups of seven beginning with <s>Kṛttikā</s> (Bahulā), proceeding from the east,
the staff of the extremely fierce one [<s>Agni</s>] stands crosswise in the direction of wind and fire;

children.text: surapatir api kṛcchraṃ yāti taṃ laṃghayitvā
children.translated_text: even the lord of the gods goes to difficulty by transgressing it —
indeed there is hostility in those directions where there is only the staff.

children.text: prāgdvārikair analadiṅ na virodham eti śeṣāḥ pradakṣiṇagatāḥ vidiśaḥ prakalpyāḥ/
children.translated_text: Those of the eastern gate do not encounter hostility in the direction of fire; the rest are to be assigned going clockwise through the intermediate directions;

children.text: ullaṃghya daṇḍam api kāmam iyān narendraḥ śūlaṃ vihāya yadi diṅmukhalagnaśuddhiḥ//
children.translated_text: even transgressing the staff, a king may go at will, abandoning the trident, if the direction, the sign at the cusp, and the ascendant are pure.
On <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Bali</s>, having gone toward the direction of <s>Puruhūta</s> (<s>Indra</s>), attained bondage;

children.text: yāmyām ājapade muraś calitavān yāto murārer vaśam/
children.translated_text: on a southern <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Aja</s>'s quarter, <s>Mura</s> set forth and came under the power of <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>);

children.text: rohiṇyāṃ namuciḥ pratīcy abhigataḥ pūrtiṃ gato vajriṇā
children.translated_text: on <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Namuci</s>, having gone westward, was fulfilled [i.e., destroyed] by the Thunderbolt-wielder (<s>Indra</s>);

children.text: saumyām aryamadaivate ca gatavān mṛtyor vaśaṃ śambaraḥ//
children.translated_text: and on the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Aryaman</s> in the northern direction, <s>Śambara</s> came under the power of death.

children.text: puṣyo 'tha hastaḥ śravaṇaḥ śraviṣṭhā prācyādimukhyāny udag aśviyuk ca/
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, and <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s> (Dhaniṣṭhā) are the chief ones for the east and other [directions], with <s>Aśvinī</s> also for the north;

children.text: naiśākaraṃ tvāṣṭram athānurādhā pauṣṇaṃ ca madhyāni tathāhur eke//
children.translated_text: some say <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, and <s>Revatī</s> are the intermediate ones.
Those designated as belonging to all gates are Jupiter's <s>nakṣatra</s> (<s>Puṣya</s>), <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, and <s>Anurādhā</s>;
the eight best are always <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, together with the first [four];
travel is condemned on <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Bharaṇī</s>, <s>Svāti</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s>, <s>Kṛttikā</s>, and <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>;
also between <s>Citrā</s> and <s>Svāti</s>, and between <s>Kṛttikā</s> and <s>Bharaṇī</s>, and between <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s> and <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>.

children.text: sve sve karmaṇi pūjitāni munibhiḥ śuddhāni sarvāṇy api
children.translated_text: All [<s>nakṣatras</s>] are pure when honored in their own respective activities, according to the sages;
except at sunrise on <s>Kṛttikā</s>, a military expedition in the direction of fire against the enemy's territory is auspicious;

children.text: rohiṇyāṃ triṣu cottareṣu vijayo yātur viśākhāsu ca
children.translated_text: on <s>Rohiṇī</s> and the three <s>Uttara</s> [<s>nakṣatras</s>], and also on <s>Viśākhā</s>, there is victory for the traveler
Abandoning the first half of the day, <s>Garga</s> declared for one seeking supreme sovereignty:

For slaying enemies, one should march in <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Indu</s> (i.e. <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>), <s>Rāga</s> (i.e. <s>Rohiṇī</s>), and <s>Śaṅkara</s> (i.e. <s>Ārdrā</s>) <s>nakṣatras</s>, excluding the first half of the day,

For the sake of servants, in <s>Pavana</s> (i.e. <s>Svāti</s>), <s>Aśvin</s> (i.e. <s>Aśvinī</s>), <s>Sūrya</s> (i.e. <s>Kṛttikā</s>), and <s>Guru</s> (i.e. <s>Puṣya</s>) <s>nakṣatras</s>, excluding the latter half of the day,

children.text: rātryādau tu na pauṣṇamaitraśaśibhatvāṣṭreṣu vāṃchan dyutiṃ
children.translated_text: At the beginning of the night, one desiring glory should not march in <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (i.e. <s>Revatī</s>), <s>Maitra</s> (i.e. <s>Anurādhā</s>), <s>Śaśibha</s> (i.e. <s>Śravaṇa</s>), and <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> (i.e. <s>Citrā</s>) <s>nakṣatras</s>,

children.text: rātrer madhyam apāsya pūrvabharaṇīpitryeṣu hantuṃ parāḥ//
children.translated_text: Avoiding the middle of the night, one should march to slay enemies in <s>Pūrva</s> (i.e. <s>Pūrvaphālgunī</s>), <s>Bharaṇī</s>, and <s>Pitrya</s> (i.e. <s>Maghā</s>) <s>nakṣatras</s>.

children.text: niśāntabhāge triṣu vaiṣṇavādyeṣv iyād dhanārthī na punarvasau ca/
children.translated_text: At the end of the night, one seeking wealth should march in the three <s>nakṣatras</s> beginning with <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (i.e. <s>Śravaṇa</s>), but not in <s>Punarvasu</s>,
Some authorities prohibit for the <s>nakṣatra</s> called <s>Ambupa</s> (i.e. <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>) the midday and the end-of-night period.
Marching at any desired time is auspicious in <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Indava</s> (i.e. <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>), <s>Upendra</s> (i.e. <s>Śravaṇa</s>), and <s>Surejya</s> (i.e. <s>Puṣya</s>) <s>nakṣatras</s>,

children.text: kṛtvā prayāṇaṃ śravaṇe śriyo 'rthī viśen na jātuḥ kṣitipaḥ svasīmni//
children.translated_text: Having set out under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, a king seeking prosperity should never re-enter his own territory.

children.text: saumye gatvādhyuṣya raudre 'ditīśe saṃprasthātā bādhate śatrusaṃghān/
children.translated_text: Having marched under <s>Saumya</s> (i.e. <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>) and halting under <s>Raudra</s> (i.e. <s>Ārdrā</s>) or <s>Aditīśa</s> (i.e. <s>Punarvasu</s>), one who then sets forth overwhelms the enemy hosts,

children.text: maitre gatvā pauruhūte samuṣya? mūle yāyāc chatrunāśāya bhūpaḥ//
children.translated_text: Having marched under <s>Maitra</s> (i.e. <s>Anurādhā</s>) and halting under <s>Pauruhūta</s> (i.e. <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>), the king should march under <s>Mūla</s> for the destruction of enemies.

children.text: haste gatvā svāticitre samuṣya śakrāgnyṛkṣe prasthito bādhate 'rīn/
children.translated_text: Having marched under <s>Hasta</s> and halting under <s>Svāti</s> or <s>Citrā</s>, one who sets forth under <s>Śakra</s> (i.e. <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>) or <s>Agni</s> (i.e. <s>Kṛttikā</s>) <s>nakṣatra</s> overwhelms the enemies,

children.text: tiṣye pauṣṇe vāsave caikarātraṃ sīmni sthitvā bhūtim āpnoti yātā//
children.translated_text: Having stayed one night within his own territory under <s>Tiṣya</s> (i.e. <s>Puṣya</s>), <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (i.e. <s>Revatī</s>), or <s>Vāsava</s> (i.e. <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>), the marcher attains prosperity.

children.text: ṛkṣe pāpaiḥ saṃyute 'ntaḥ prakopo lakṣmībhraṃśo rāhuṇārkeṇa rogaḥ/
children.translated_text: When the <s>nakṣatra</s> is conjoined with <s>pāpa</s> (malefic) <s>grahas</s>, there is internal revolt; with <s>Rāhu</s>, loss of fortune; with <s>Arka</s> (i.e. <s>Sūrya</s>), disease;

children.text: ketūlkābhyāṃ pīḍite deśanāśaḥ kleśaḥ saure soṣṇaraśmyātmaje ca//
children.translated_text: When afflicted by <s>Ketu</s> or a meteor, destruction of the kingdom; when by <s>Śani</s> (i.e. <s>Saturn</s>) together with <s>Uṣṇaraśmi</s>'s son (i.e. <s>Maṅgala</s>), there is distress.
When the <s>nakṣatras</s> are associated with directional portents, smoke, halos, earthquakes, and dust storms, then hardship, disease, exhaustion, and afflictions from calamity arise,

children.text: bhinne graheṇa vaśatām upayāti śatroḥ sandhyārātre 'śanihate 'javighāta uktaḥ//
children.translated_text: When pierced by a <s>graha</s>, one falls under the enemy's power; when afflicted by lightning at the twilight-night, it is said to cause sudden destruction.

children.text: janmādi karma tato dṛśan na(va)maṃ saṃghātikaṃ coḍubhāgam/
children.translated_text: The <s>janma</s> (birth) <s>nakṣatra</s> is the first; <s>karma</s> (action) is then the tenth; <s>dṛśa</s> (sight) is the ninth; <s>saṃghātika</s> (collective) is the division of the <s>nakṣatra</s>;
<s>Samudaya</s> (rise) is counted from the first as the tenth; and that called <s>bhramavināśa</s> (destruction through confusion) is the twenty-third.

children.text: ādyāt tu paṃcaviṃśaṃ mānasametaṃ naraḥ ṣaḍṛkṣaḥ syāt/
children.translated_text: The twenty-fifth from the first is called <s>mānasameta</s> (endowed with honor); a man has six significant <s>nakṣatras</s>,
The king whose <s>nakṣatra</s> is the <s>mānavanakṣatra</s> — that same one, counted from the first, is his <s>abhiṣeka-ṛkṣa</s> (coronation <s>nakṣatra</s>).
The good or bad result of these is in accordance with their names, through the merits and defects of benefic and malefic qualities,
When the <s>janma-ṛkṣa</s> (birth-star) and the rest are purified, the marcher conquers enemies swiftly.
The <s>janma</s> (birth), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>ādhāna</s> (conception) <s>nakṣatras</s>, when rising, produce prosperity, adversity, and well-being respectively;
They become <s>pratyari</s> (hostile), <s>sādhaka</s> (accomplishing), <s>vaināśika</s> (destructive); and also <s>mitra</s> (friendly) and <s>atimitra</s> (very friendly).
The <s>mitra</s>, <s>atimitra</s>, <s>sādhaka</s>, and <s>sampad</s> (prosperity) <s>nakṣatras</s> are auspicious, as is the <s>karma-bha</s> (action-star);
One who marches does not obtain the remainder; but before the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (coronation), one who marches succeeds.
Having bathed with white mustard, <s>siddhārthaka</s>, rice, <s>priyaṅgu</s>, <s>madayantikā</s>, and water under <s>Puṣya</s>,
One should march eastward; under <s>Saumya</s> (i.e. <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>), with waters containing a thousand gems.
With waters mixed with earth from a cow's horn, a riverbank, a mountain, an anthill, a tank, and substances of the dead,

children.text: toyaiḥ snātvā nṛpatir yāyād yāmyāṃ diśaṃ haste//
children.translated_text: Having bathed, the king should march toward the southern direction under <s>Hasta</s>.
Having bathed with earth from turbulent rivers under <s>Caitra</s> (i.e. <s>Citrā</s>), one should march toward the eastern direction,
Under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, with waters containing earth from river confluences, one should march westward.
Having bathed with waters mixed with honey, <s>bhadradāru</s> (deodar), one should march northward under <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s> (i.e. <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>),
With vessels of cow and elephant horn filled with honey and ghee, one should go northward under <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (i.e. <s>Revatī</s>),
Northward indeed under <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (i.e. <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>), having bathed with waters filled with honey and <s>pūthikā</s>,
And having offered oblations to <s>Agni</s> with <s>nakṣatra</s> deity <s>mantras</s>, one obtains victory.

children.text: akṣatamāṣāḥ khinnās tilasahitās taṇḍulā dadhi ca gavyam/
children.translated_text: Unbroken rice grains, <s>māṣa</s> beans, fatigued (parched) grains, sesame seeds, rice, curds, and cow's products,
And the flesh of a bull and of a deer — these are the offerings for the five <s>nakṣatras</s> beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s>.
Blood, liquid offerings, <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice), and serpent flesh are for those beginning with <s>Śaṅkara</s> (i.e. <s>Ārdrā</s>),
For <s>Pitrya</s> (i.e. <s>Maghā</s>), sesame-rice; for the next pair of <s>nakṣatras</s>, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice.

children.text: prāśyāḥ priyaṅgucitrāṇḍajāḥ phalaṃ yāvakaṃ kulatthāś ca/
children.translated_text: One should eat <s>priyaṅgu</s>, variegated eggs, fruits, barley gruel, and <s>kulattha</s> beans,

children.text: madhusarpiṣī ca hastān mūlāny ambūni saktavo mūlāt//
children.translated_text: Also honey and ghee from <s>Hasta</s>; roots, waters, and barley meal from <s>Mūla</s>.

children.text: śravaṇādīnām adyāc chāliṃ śākaṃ biḍālamāṃsaṃ ca/
children.translated_text: For those beginning with <s>Śravaṇa</s>, one should eat rice, vegetables, and cat's flesh,
Ghee, any desired meat, and barley meal mixed with <s>māṣa</s> beans.

children.text: prāśyādi ghṛtaṃ tilaudanaṃ matsyāḥ kṣīram iti pradakṣiṇam/
children.translated_text: One should eat ghee, sesame-rice, fish, and milk in clockwise order as the primary offerings,

children.text: adyān nṛpatir yathādiśaṃ nakṣatrābhihitaṃ ca siddhaye//
children.translated_text: The king should eat according to the direction and as prescribed by the <s>nakṣatra</s>, for the sake of success.

children.text: asvādu cyutakacamakṣikānuviddhaṃ durgandhi kṣayakṛd abhūri yac ca dagdham/
children.translated_text: Food that is tasteless, stale, contaminated by hair or flies, foul-smelling, decayed, scanty, or burnt is inauspicious;

children.text: susvinnaṃ mudu ruciraṃ manonukūlaṃ svādvannaṃ bahu vijayāya yānakāle//
children.translated_text: Food that is well-cooked, soft, beautiful, pleasing to the mind, sweet, and abundant leads to victory at the time of marching.

children.text: guṇavati tithāv ṛkṣe 'niṣṭe divā gamanaṃ hitaṃ
children.translated_text: When the <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) is auspicious but the <s>nakṣatra</s> is inauspicious, daytime marching is beneficial,

children.text: niśi ca bhagane śastaṃ yānaṃ tithau guṇavarjite/
children.translated_text: And when the <s>nakṣatra</s> is auspicious but the <s>tithi</s> is devoid of good qualities, marching at night is recommended,
One who goes contrary to this obtains the defects declared by the <s>nakṣatra</s> and <s>tithi</s>,

children.text: guṇam api tayoḥ samyag yātur jagāda bhṛgur muniḥ//E30
children.translated_text: And the sage <s>Bhṛgu</s> has declared that one who marches correctly obtains the combined merits of both.
Chapter 5: Results of the Weekdays
One who marches on the day of <s>Savitṛ</s> (i.e. <s>Sunday</s>) suffers stomach ailments, eye diseases, wild animals, forest dangers, and loss of wealth,

children.text: anilakaphajarogān śaktimānānnahāniṃ salilajanitapīḍāṃ cāhni yātā himāṃśoḥ//
children.translated_text: One who marches on the day of <s>Himāṃśu</s> (i.e. <s>Monday</s>) suffers diseases of wind and phlegm, loss of strength and food, and afflictions caused by water.
One who marches on the day of <s>Avani</s> (i.e. <s>Tuesday</s>) suffers fire, violence, poison, blood ailments, bilious disease, enemy affliction, and is harassed by enemy hosts,

children.text: ahani savitṛsūnor dainyam āpnoti gacchan svajanadhanaviyogaṃ mṛtyubandhāmayāṃś ca//
children.translated_text: One who marches on the day of <s>Savitṛsūnu</s> (i.e. <s>Saturday</s>) obtains wretchedness, separation from kinsmen and wealth, death, imprisonment, and diseases.

children.text: budhadivasagato 'rīn bādhate mantraśaktyā sravaṇasukhakathāptiṃ śilpimitrāgamāṃś ca/
children.translated_text: One who goes on <s>Budha</s>'s day (i.e. <s>Wednesday</s>) overcomes enemies by the power of <s>mantras</s>, and obtains the pleasure of hearing, good tidings, arts, and the arrival of friends,

children.text: kṣitidhanajayaratnastrīpratāpapramodān atibalam acireṇa svīkaroty ahni sūreḥ//
children.translated_text: On the day of <s>Sūri</s> (i.e. <s>Thursday</s>), one quickly acquires through great strength: land, wealth, victory, gems, women, glory, and delight.
On the day of <s>Sita</s> (i.e. <s>Friday</s>), one enjoys excellent women, beds, garments, perfumes, food, drink, amorous pleasures, wealth, and gems,

children.text: anupacayagato 'haḥ śastam apy apraśastaṃ śubham upacayasaṃsthaḥ pāpasaṃjño vidhatte//E4
children.translated_text: A day-lord placed in a non-<s>upacaya</s> (non-increasing) house makes even an auspicious day inauspicious; one of malefic designation placed in an <s>upacaya</s> (increasing) house produces auspicious results.
Chapter 6: <s>Muhūrta</s> (Auspicious Moments)
The <s>karaṇas</s> (half-lunar-days) are favorable for the marcher, excluding <s>Gara</s>, <s>Vaṇij</s>, and <s>Viṣṭi</s>,

children.text: garam api kaiś cic chastaṃ vaṇijaṃ ca vaṇikkriyāsv eva/
children.translated_text: Though some consider <s>Gara</s> auspicious, and <s>Vaṇij</s> only in commercial activities.

The daytime <s>muhūrtas</s> are presided over by <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Bhujaga</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Pitṛ</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, <s>Jala</s>, <s>Viśva</s>, <s>Viriñci</s>, and <s>Paṅkajaprabha</s> (i.e. <s>Brahmā</s>),
Then <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s> again, <s>Niśācara</s> (i.e. <s>Rākṣasa</s>), <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, and <s>Yoni</s> — these are the daytime <s>muhūrtas</s>.
The nighttime <s>muhūrtas</s> are: <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Aja</s>, <s>Ahirbudhnya</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Dasra</s> (i.e. <s>Aśvin</s>), <s>Antaka</s> (i.e. <s>Yama</s>), <s>Agni</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>,

Then <s>Indu</s> (i.e. <s>Soma</s>), <s>Aditi</s>, <s>Guru</s> (i.e. <s>Bṛhaspati</s>), <s>Hari</s> (i.e. <s>Viṣṇu</s>), <s>Ravi</s> (i.e. <s>Sūrya</s>), <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, and <s>Anila</s> (i.e. <s>Vāyu</s>) — these are the nighttime <s>muhūrtas</s>.

children.text: ahnaḥ pañcadaśāṃśo rātreś caivaṃ muhūrta iti saṃjñā//
children.translated_text: A <s>muhūrta</s> is defined as one-fifteenth part of the day, and likewise of the night.

children.text: sa ca vijñeyas tajjñaiś chāyāyantrāmbubhir yuktyā//
children.translated_text: It should be determined by experts through shadow-instruments and water-clocks, by calculation.

children.text: nakṣatravat kṣaṇānaṃ parighādi tadīśvaraiḥ samaṃ cintyaṃ/
children.translated_text: The <s>parigha</s> and other such factors of the <s>muhūrtas</s>, together with their presiding deities, should be considered just as for <s>nakṣatras</s>,

children.text: phalam api tad eva dṛṣṭaṃ gargādyais tatra ca ślokāḥ//
children.translated_text: The same results have been observed by <s>Garga</s> and other authorities; and on this topic, the verses are:
The complete day-and-night cycle is joined with the <s>Candra-nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion),
And the <s>muhūrtas</s> of that <s>nakṣatra</s> are declared to have the same qualities as the corresponding actions.

children.text: aṣṭame 'rdhadivase same śubho yo viriñcavibhusaṃjñitaḥ kṣaṇaḥ/
children.translated_text: At the eighth half-day, the even <s>muhūrta</s> called <s>Viriñci</s> (i.e. <s>Brahmā</s>) and <s>Vibhu</s> is auspicious;

children.text: tena yānam apahāya dakṣiṇāṃ sarvadikṣv abhijitā praśasyate//E7
children.translated_text: Avoiding the southern direction, marching during that <s>muhūrta</s> or during <s>Abhijit</s> is praised in all directions.
Chapter 7: Strength of the <s>Moon</s>

children.text: satya āha gatikarmakalpahā janmagas tu himaguryiyāsataḥ/
children.translated_text: <s>Satya</s> declared that the <s>Moon</s> in transit destroys the effects of <s>karma</s> (action); but when situated in the birth <s>nakṣatra</s>, it hinders the one wishing to march,

children.text: tatra dehanavate 'vajāyate tena karmasu na sādhakaḥ smṛtaḥ//
children.translated_text: For in that position the body's strength wanes; therefore it is declared not to be a promoter of success in undertakings.

children.text: tac ca tasya bahubhir viśodhitaṃ lagnam eva sutarāṃ yatas tanuḥ/
children.translated_text: This has been extensively examined by many authorities; the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant) is especially important since it represents the body,

children.text: tulyadehanavatāṃ prapadya kiṃ sodayodayam uvāca śobhanam//
children.translated_text: For those having the same body-strength, what does one gain? He declared the coincidence of rising to be auspicious.
When the <s>Moon</s>, purified through the <s>aṣṭavarga</s> system, attains the state of excellence,

children.text: janmago 'pi hi tadā praśasyate yo 'ṣṭavargaśubhadaḥ sa śobhanaḥ//
children.translated_text: Even when situated in the birth <s>nakṣatra</s>, it is praiseworthy; that which gives auspicious results in the <s>aṣṭavarga</s> is indeed beneficial.
The <s>Moon</s> situated in the seventh, eighth, tenth, sixth, third, or birth <s>nakṣatra</s> does not give desired results when <s>grahas</s> occupy the second or eighth houses;
But it gives desired results when <s>grahas</s> are in the fourth, first, eleventh, ninth, or fifth houses, provided it occupies the opposite sign.

children.text: yasya gocaraphalapramāṇatā tasya vedhaphalam iṣyate na vā/
children.translated_text: For one whose <s>gocara</s> (transit) results are authoritative, is the <s>vedha</s> (obstruction) result desired or not?

children.text: prāyaśo na bahusaṃmataṃ tv idaṃ sthūlamārgaphalado hi gocaraḥ//
children.translated_text: For the most part, this is not accepted by many authorities, since <s>gocara</s> gives only broad general results.

children.text: yasyotsṛjaty uḍupatiḥ puruṣo 'pasavyaṃ janmarkṣam āpadam upaiti sa bhūmipālaḥ/
children.translated_text: The king whose birth <s>nakṣatra</s> the <s>Moon</s> leaves in an anticlockwise direction encounters calamity;

children.text: yāyī tathetaragṛhopagate sitādau yāyītareś varajayo bahule kṣayaś ca//
children.translated_text: The marcher should set out when <s>Śukra</s> (i.e. <s>Venus</s>) and the like occupy the other houses; in the dark half, the enemy's defeat occurs, but also decline.

children.text: horārāśāv upacayagṛhe janmabhe vā yiyāsor hānir hānāv uḍugaṇapatau vṛddhir āpūryamāṇe/
children.translated_text: For one wishing to march, when the lord of the <s>nakṣatras</s> is in the <s>horā</s> sign, an <s>upacaya</s> (increasing) house, or the birth <s>nakṣatra</s>, there is loss during the waning phase and gain during the waxing phase,

children.text: pakṣasy ādāv apacayagṛhe hānir āpūryamāṇe vṛddhis tūktā hrasati himagau kṛṣṇapakṣādisaṃsthe//
children.translated_text: At the beginning of the fortnight, when in a non-<s>upacaya</s> house during the waxing phase there is loss, but gain is declared; when the <s>Moon</s> wanes while situated at the start of the dark fortnight, there is decline.

children.text: upacayagṛhayuktaḥ savyagaḥ śuklapakṣe śubham abhilaṣamāṇaḥ saumyamadhyasthito vā/
children.translated_text: When the <s>Moon</s> is endowed with an <s>upacaya</s> house, moving direct in the bright fortnight, one desiring auspiciousness, or when situated among benefics,

children.text: sakhivaśigṛhayuktaḥ kārakarkṣe 'pi cendur jayasukhaphaladātā tatprahartāny athātaḥ//
children.translated_text: When the <s>Moon</s> is in a friendly or subject house, or in the <s>kāraka</s> (significator) <s>nakṣatra</s>, it bestows victory and happiness; now, regarding the agents of attack:

children.text: prakṣīṇe 'pya anupacayasthite 'pe yāyād viśrabdhaṃ yadi sakhivaśyakārakarkṣe/
children.translated_text: Even when waning, even when in a non-<s>upacaya</s> position, one may march confidently if the <s>Moon</s> is in a friendly, subject, or <s>kāraka</s> <s>nakṣatra</s>;

children.text: naivaṃ ced udayagṛhāt svajanmabhād vā sampūrṇe 'py upacayage 'pi na prayāyāt//
children.translated_text: If this is not the case, one should not march even when the <s>Moon</s> is full and in an <s>upacaya</s> position, counting from the rising sign or one's birth <s>nakṣatra</s>.

children.text: bhṛgusutabudhabhinne ruk sureḍyena mṛtyur bhayam asitakujābhyāṃ ketunā strīpraṇāśaḥ/
children.translated_text: When the <s>Moon</s> is afflicted by <s>Bhṛgusuta</s> (i.e. <s>Śukra</s>) or <s>Budha</s>, there is illness; by <s>Surejya</s> (i.e. <s>Guru</s>), death; by <s>Asita</s> (i.e. <s>Śani</s>) and <s>Kuja</s> (i.e. <s>Maṅgala</s>), fear; by <s>Ketu</s>, destruction of wife;

children.text: apaṭukiraṇakāntau gacchataḥ śatruvṛddhiḥ savikṛtapariveṣe netranāśaḥ śaśāṅke//E10
children.translated_text: When <s>Apaṭukiraṇa</s> (i.e. <s>Rāhu</s>) and <s>Kānti</s> (i.e. <s>Moon</s>) move together, there is increase of enemies; when the <s>Moon</s> has a distorted halo, there is destruction of the eyes.
Chapter 8: Strength of the <s>Lagna</s> (Ascendant)

children.text: dvipadavaśagāḥ sarve siṃhaṃ vihāya catuṣpadāḥ salilanilayābharkṣāvaśyāḥ sarīsṛpajātayaḥ/
children.translated_text: All biped signs are subject to bipeds, excluding <s>Siṃha</s> (Leo); the quadruped signs control quadrupeds; aquatic and <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpio) signs control reptile species,

children.text: mṛgapativaśe tiṣṭhanty ete vihāya sarīsṛpān na kathitagṛheṣūhyaṃ vaśyaṃ janavyavahārataḥ//
children.translated_text: These stand under the dominion of <s>Mṛgapati</s> (i.e. <s>Leo</s>), excluding the reptiles; the subject relationship in the stated houses is determined by popular convention.

children.text: sthalajalajasarīsṛpāḥ svakānāṃ balam abhivīkṣya vidheyatāṃ bhajante/
children.translated_text: The land-born, aquatic, and reptile signs serve their own kind, observing the strength of their own;

children.text: viṣamagṛhavaśe samā dyusaṃsthā niśi viṣamā vaśavartinaḥ samānām//
children.translated_text: Odd signs rule when the <s>lagna</s> is in the daytime, even signs at night — these are the subject relationships of their respective groups.

children.text: śīrṣodaye samabhivāṃchitakāryasiddhiḥ pṛṣṭhodaye viphalatāṃ balavidravaś ca/
children.translated_text: When a sign rises head-first, there is accomplishment of the desired objective; when it rises tail-first, there is failure and dispersal of forces,

children.text: yātavyadiṅmukhagatasya sukhena siddhir vyarthaśramo bhavati dikpratilomalagen//
children.translated_text: When the <s>lagna</s> faces the direction of intended travel, there is easy success; when the <s>lagna</s> is in the opposite direction, the effort is fruitless.

children.text: śastaṃ divā dinabale niśi naktavīrye rāśau viparyayabale gamanaṃ na śastam/
children.translated_text: Marching by day when the day-strong sign is rising, and at night when the night-strong sign is rising, is auspicious; marching when the strength is reversed is not recommended,
When the <s>Moon</s>, <s>Sun</s>, and <s>lagna</s> are conjoined in movable and other signs at the time of departure, they bestow increase through others, one's own, or both, of the kingdom.

children.text: mīnodaye pravasataḥ kuṭilaḥ sadoṣo mārge bhavaty akṛtakāryanivartanam ca/
children.translated_text: When <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces) is rising, the traveler's path becomes crooked and faulty, and there is return without accomplishing the objective,

children.text: anyāṃśakeṣv api jhaṣe phalam etad eva mīnāṃśakeṣu ca pararkṣasamāśriteṣu//
children.translated_text: This same result applies even when other signs occupy the <s>Mīna</s> <s>navāṃśa</s> (Pisces subdivision), and when <s>Mīna</s> subdivisions occupy other rising signs.

children.text: ripunidhane ripunidhanaṃ ripuṣaṣṭhe lagnage vadho yātuḥ/
children.translated_text: When the enemy's eighth house occupies the enemy's eighth, or when the enemy's sixth occupies the <s>lagna</s>, there is death of the marcher;
This is the teaching of <s>Satya</s> in the <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> tradition, but this is not absolute.

children.text: śatroḥ prasūtisamaye yadi nidhanaṃ saṃyutaṃ grahaiḥ pāpaiḥ/
children.translated_text: If at the time of the enemy's birth, the eighth house is conjoined with malefic <s>grahas</s>,

children.text: saumyayutaṃ vā ṣaṣṭhaṃ sadasatphalatā tatas tābhyām//
children.translated_text: Or the sixth is conjoined with benefics, then good or bad results follow accordingly from those two.

children.text: kleśād vinā phalam arikṣayam arthasiddhiṃ prāpnoti lagnasahite pravasan svalagne/
children.translated_text: One who travels when the <s>lagna</s> is conjoined with one's own birth-sign obtains the result of enemy destruction and success without hardship,

children.text: arthakṣayaṃ śramamanarthamato dvitīye kalyāṇasaukhyavibhavāgamam āhur eke//
children.translated_text: In the second house, loss of wealth, toil, and misfortune; some say the attainment of welfare, happiness, and prosperity.
In the third house: gain of servants, wealth, vehicles, allies, and victory; in the fourth: imprisonment, loss of wealth, fear, and destruction of the army,
In the fifth house (the child's sign): increase of enemies through <s>mantra</s>-chanting and calamity; in the sixth: gain of the enemy's wealth, strength, splendor, and victory.

children.text: dyūne 'dhvavāhanavipatkṣudatiśramārtir bandho vadhaḥ paribhavo nidhane rujaś ca/
children.translated_text: In the seventh: road hazards, vehicle mishaps, hunger, excessive exhaustion and pain; in the eighth: imprisonment, death, humiliation, and diseases,

children.text: dharme 'rthanāśagadakāryavipadbhayāni kāryaṃ vinā balabhayaṃ daśame kṣayaś ca//
children.translated_text: In the ninth: loss of wealth, illness, failure of purpose, and dangers; in the tenth: fear despite strength and decline, without accomplishing the objective.

children.text: kecid vadanty upacayopagṛhītam etat tasmāc chubhaṃ daśamabhe gamanaṃ vilagen/
children.translated_text: Some say this should be understood with reference to <s>upacaya</s> (increasing) houses; therefore, marching when the <s>lagna</s> is in the tenth sign is auspicious,

children.text: arthāptidīptiśubhasiddhijayāś ca lābhe ripphe chalaṃ vyaaybhaye vijite 'pi bhedaḥ//
children.translated_text: In the eleventh: gain of wealth, splendor, auspicious success, and victory; in the twelfth: deceit, fear of expenditure, and even when victorious, there is division.
When the birth-sign rises, there is death of a son due to illness and failure; in its fifth,

children.text: dyūne kleśam avāpya janmabhavanāt prāpnoti paścāt sukham/
children.translated_text: In the seventh, after experiencing distress from the birth house, one obtains happiness afterwards,
In the ninth sign, there is return from the road itself; in <s>Meṣūraṇa</s> (i.e. the tenth), gain of wealth;

children.text: śeṣarkṣeṣu yathaiva lagnabhavanāt tadvat phalaṃ janmataḥ//
children.translated_text: In the remaining signs, the results from the birth-sign are the same as those from the <s>lagna</s>.
When <s>Sūrya</s> (the <s>Sun</s>) occupies the rising <s>lagna</s>: hunger, thirst, suffering, loss of path, eye disease, and distress,

children.text: śastā cāndre devatārthaṃ svadeśe kauje pittavyālaśastrāgnipīḍā//
children.translated_text: When <s>Candra</s> (the <s>Moon</s>) is there, it is auspicious for religious purposes in one's own land; when <s>Kuja</s> (i.e. <s>Maṅgala</s>), affliction from bile, serpents, weapons, and fire,

children.text: baudhe tuṣṭir vāṃchitāptir yaśaś ca jaive 'thāptiḥ sthānamānārināśāḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>Budha</s> (i.e. <s>Mercury</s>) is there: satisfaction, attainment of desires, and fame; when <s>Guru</s> (i.e. <s>Jupiter</s>): gain of wealth, position, honor, and destruction of enemies,

children.text: strīratnāptiḥ kāryasiddhiś ca śaukre mānde bandhavyādhinīcāvamānāḥ//
children.translated_text: When <s>Śukra</s> (i.e. <s>Venus</s>) is there: gain of women and gems, and success in undertakings; when <s>Śani</s> (i.e. <s>Saturn</s>): bondage, illness, humiliation, and disgrace,

children.text: saumyo 'pi janmani na yaḥ śubhapuṣṭidātā sthānaṃ na tasya śubhadaṃ vrajato vilagen/
children.translated_text: Even a benefic <s>graha</s> that does not give auspicious and nourishing results in the birth <s>nakṣatra</s> — its position does not bestow good for one traveling with the <s>lagna</s>.

children.text: pāpo 'pi yaḥ śubhaphalaṃ prakaroti puṃsāṃ sthānaṃ vilagnagatam iṣṭam uśanti tasya//
children.translated_text: Even a malefic planet that produces auspicious results for a person—they declare that its station, when placed in the ascendant, is favorable.
That house which is not amenable [i.e., the 6th, 8th, or 12th] with respect to the traveler's birth-sign and ascendant-sign,
even if the ascendant is favorable, becomes one that causes loss of wealth and fatigue.
When the ascendant sign is in a friendly and submissive relationship with the traveler's birth-sign and ascendant-sign,
even if it is a decreasing [house], the traveler quickly [obtains] victory, wealth, honor, and income.

children.text: kecid vadanti yasmin graho niraṃśaṃ karoti tallagnam/
children.translated_text: Some say that the ascendant in which a planet has zero degrees [i.e., is at the very beginning of a sign],
that house is unfavorable for the traveler, causing fear, grief, and distress.

children.text: vṛṣavṛścikakarkaṭair nṛṇām anukūlair api lagnam āśritaiḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpio), and <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer) occupy the ascendant, even if favorable for a person,
the sages declare the journey inauspicious, and likewise when occupied by other signs.

children.text: veśirvilagnopagato yiyāsor vināpi yatnāt kurute phalāptim/
children.translated_text: When <s>Veśī</s> [a specific yoga] occupies the ascendant, the traveler, even without effort, obtains results.

children.text: gauyānam iṣṭaṃ jalarāśilagne tad aṃśake cānyagṛhodaye 'pi//E20
children.translated_text: A water-sign in the ascendant is favorable for a water-journey, and also when its <s>aṃśaka</s> (subdivision) [is a water-sign], even when another house is rising.
Chapter 9: Divisions of the Ascendant (<s>lagnabheda</s>)

children.text: ūrdhvā tiryag vānatā syāc ca horā muktā krāntā nāgatārkā krameṇa/
children.translated_text: The <s>horā</s> (half-sign) is upward, transverse, downward, free, passing, not-yet-arrived, and solar, in order.

children.text: ity etāḥ syur jīvaśarmopadeśe jñeyo rāśir brahmaṣaṇḍasya pakṣe//
children.translated_text: These are according to the teaching of <s>Jīvaśarman</s>; in the view of <s>Brahmaṣaṇḍa</s>, the [entire] sign should be understood [as the horā].

children.text: ūrdhvā syād yā ṣaṭcarādyeṣu horā bhūyo bhūyo maṇḍale kaiścid uktā/
children.translated_text: The upward <s>horā</s> is the one in the first six signs; by some it is stated to recur again and again in the cycle.

children.text: rāśau rāśau prāgvilagnopayātaiḥ drekkāṇais tu prāha horāṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ//
children.translated_text: In each sign, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> determines the <s>horā</s> by the <s>drekkāṇas</s> (decans) that have approached the eastern ascendant.

children.text: sarvaṃ pramāṇaṃ municoditatvāt kiṃ tv atra yojyaṃ dalam eva horā/
children.translated_text: Everything is authoritative because it is taught by sages; however, what is to be applied here is only the half-sign (<s>dala</s>) as the <s>horā</s>.

children.text: yasmin sahasrāṃśuravasthito 'rdhe tiryaṅmukhī sā gaṇaye tato 'nyāḥ//
children.translated_text: The half in which the thousand-rayed one (the Sun) is situated—that is transverse-facing; from that I reckon the others.

children.text: dhatte vāṃchitakāryam ūrdhvavadanā kleśād vinā lagnagā
children.translated_text: The upward-facing [<s>horā</s>], when in the ascendant, grants the desired goal without difficulty;
the transverse-facing one causes hardship, fatigue, and loss for the traveler;

children.text: sainyabhraṃśam adhomukhī prakurute kṛcchrād gṛhe cāgamaṃ
children.translated_text: the downward-facing one causes the rout of the army and a difficult return home;

children.text: srvāḥ puṣṭaphalapradāḥ svapatinā dṛṣṭā na pāpagrahaiḥ//
children.translated_text: all [<s>horās</s>] give abundant results when aspected by their own lord and not by malefic planets.

children.text: grahadivasaphalaṃ yad eva yātur tad akhilam eva karoti tasya horā/
children.translated_text: Whatever result is [predicted] for a planet's day for the traveler, the <s>horā</s> produces entirely the same for him.
Some say that [the <s>horā</s>] of the cold-water-creator (the Moon) grants women, jewels, and comfort without harm; and so does the lunar [<s>horā</s>].
One should assign results resembling the form, activity, and qualities of the <s>drekkāṇa</s> (decan) for the sake of prosperity.
When the <s>drekkāṇa</s> has a pleasant form, endowed with flowers and fruits and accompanied by gems and vessels,

children.text: saumyair dṛṣṭe jayaḥ syāt praharaṇasahite pāpadṛṣṭe ca bhaṅgaḥ
children.translated_text: and aspected by benefics, there is victory; when equipped with weapons and aspected by malefics, there is defeat.

children.text: sāgnau dāho 'tha bandhaḥ sabhujaganigale pāśayukte ca yātuḥ//
children.translated_text: When [the <s>drekkāṇa</s> is] with fire, there is burning; when with a bound serpent at the neck, there is imprisonment and binding with a noose for the traveler.

children.text: nṛpabhūrtir lagnagate drekkāṇe mantriṇo dvitīye ca/
children.translated_text: When the <s>drekkāṇa</s> in the ascendant [indicates] the king's share, in the second the minister's,
in the third the physician, the family priest, and the astrologer; in the remaining [drekkāṇas], the servants.
Position, valor, planning, occupation, military strength—
food, and bed and seat—these in the five [houses], respectively.
Conveyance, seat, bed, and vehicles in the tenth; in the next, food and drink;
vehicles and warriors after that; in the thirteenth is the crown prince.

children.text: jñeyaṃ balaṃ prayātur mantrasya viniścayaś ca tatparatah/
children.translated_text: The strength of the traveler should be known, and the determination of counsel after that;
from the fifteenth onward, in the first group of four <s>drekkāṇas</s>, the enemies.
In the nineteenth, the army's encampment on water; after that, wealth; after that, purposes;
after that, the army's commander; after that, the army's troubles.
After that, the army's vulnerabilities; the army commander comes in the twenty-fourth.

children.text: sainyārogyaṃ sainyaṃ catuṣpadaṃ ca kramāt tritaye//
children.translated_text: The army's health, the army, and quadrupeds—in order, in three.

children.text: kāryaṃ kośaḥ phalasiddhayas traye bhūmipās traye parataḥ/
children.translated_text: The task, the treasury, the fulfillment of results in three; the kings in three after that;
then religious ceremony, honoring the warriors, and the conclusion of the military campaign.

children.text: ity udayādyā bhāvā drekkāṇair ye mayā samuddiṣṭāḥ/
children.translated_text: Thus the houses beginning from the ascendant and the <s>drekkāṇas</s> that I have enumerated—
auspicious and inauspicious results should be predicted from seeing their auspicious and inauspicious [combinations].
When the <s>navāṃśa</s> (ninth-division) of the Sun arrives at the ascendant, there is destruction of the vehicle;
a difficult return home and diminished power; and in the Moon's <s>aṃśa</s> (division)—
in that of Mars, danger from fire; in Mercury's, attainment of friends; in Jupiter's, gain of wealth;
in Venus's, increase of enjoyments; in Saturn's <s>aṃśa</s>, destruction of servants.

children.text: yad udayati phalaṃ grahe pradiṣṭaṃ janayati tasya navāṃśako vlagne/
children.translated_text: Whatever result is prescribed for a planet rising—that same result the <s>navāṃśa</s> produces when in the ascendant.

children.text: subhabhavananavāṃśe sahāyo ripubalabhāgam upaiti yātur atra//
children.translated_text: When the <s>navāṃśa</s> is in an auspicious house, a companion [is gained]; [if in] the enemy's division, the traveler encounters [the enemy's] strength here.

children.text: yat proktaṃ rāśy udaye dvādaśabhāge 'pi tat phalaṃ vācyam/
children.translated_text: What has been stated for the rising of a sign should also be declared as the result for its twelfth part (<s>dvādaśabhāga</s>).

children.text: yac ca navāṃśakavihitaṃ triṃśāṃśasyodaye tat syāt//E18
children.translated_text: And what has been prescribed for the <s>navāṃśa</s>, that applies at the rising of the <s>triṃśāṃśa</s> (thirtieth-division).
Chapter 10: Strength of Planets by House-Position (<s>grahasthānabala</s>)
The Sun rising in the ascendant causes suffering, grief, disease, and obstacles; in the second, it takes away welfare, honor, strength, and affection;
in the third, it gives gold, food, coral, gems, and land; in the fourth, it gives dispassion, quarrel with kinsmen, displeasure, and distress.

children.text: putrāpadaṃ sutagṛhe 'dhvani cārthasiddhiṃ ṣaṣṭhe 'bhivāṃchitaphalāptim arikṣayaṃ ca/
children.translated_text: In the house of children (5th), calamity to a son; on the road (6th), success in one's purpose; in the sixth also, attainment of desired results and destruction of enemies;

children.text: dyūne kalatrakalahaṃ dhanasaṃkṣayaṃ ca mṛtyuṃ karoti nidhane savitā rujaṃ ca//
children.translated_text: in the seventh (spouse's house), quarrel with wife and loss of wealth; the Sun in the eighth (house of death) causes death, disease, and suffering.

children.text: dharmaṃ hinasti navame savitārthadaś ca hatvā viyatyaviditaṃ śramakarmadātā/
children.translated_text: In the ninth, it hinders religious merit but gives wealth; in the tenth (mid-heaven), it gives unknown and arduous work after killing;

children.text: ratnāgamaṃ subahu lābhagataḥ karoti kṛtvā vyayaṃ vyayagataḥ kurute 'rtham alpam//
children.translated_text: in the eleventh (house of gain), it brings much gain of jewels; in the twelfth (house of expenditure), having spent, it produces little wealth.

children.text: lagne śaśī kalahaśokakaro na pūrṇaḥ strīvājiratnasuhṛdātmajadaḥ kuṭumbe/
children.translated_text: The Moon in the ascendant causes quarrel and grief (if not full); in the second, it gives wife, horse, jewels, friends, and sons.

children.text: duścikyago yuvatiratnadhanapradātā bandhvāptidaḥ suhṛdi tatkṣayadaś ca kṛṣṇe//
children.translated_text: In the third, it gives women, jewels, and wealth; in the fourth (kinsmen), it gives kinsmen and relatives—but takes them away if waning.

children.text: arthapradas tanayagaḥ sutaśokakṛc ca mitrāritāṃ prakurute na sukhaṃ ca ṣaṣṭhe/
children.translated_text: In the fifth, it gives wealth but causes grief over sons, and produces enmity with friends; in the sixth, no happiness.
In the seventh, it gives wealth, land, and women; in the eighth, loss of wealth; a small Moon in the eighth causes grief over death for the traveler.

children.text: pratyeti cāśu navame kurute ca kāryaṃ kṣīṇe kṣayo viyati vṛddhirato 'nyathāsthe/
children.translated_text: In the ninth, the traveler returns quickly and accomplishes the task; when waning, there is decay; in the tenth (mid-heaven), increase—otherwise, adversity.

children.text: aiśvaryasaukhyadhanalābham upaite lābhe kleśakṣayavyayabhayāni ca riṣphayāte//
children.translated_text: In the eleventh, one attains sovereignty, happiness, wealth, and gain; in the twelfth, hardship, decay, expenditure, and fears.

children.text: lagne viṣāgnirudhirāgamaśastrabādhā bhindyād balaṃ dhanagato 'rthakaraś ca paścāt/
children.translated_text: Mars in the ascendant [causes] danger from poison, fire, blood-flow, and weapons; it may break the army; in the second, it first produces wealth;
in the third, attainment of women, jewels, wealth, and garments; in the fourth, destruction of kinsmen and fear from enemies.

children.text: putāpadaṃ kṣitisutaḥ kurute sutasthaḥ śatrupraṇāśam acirād arigaḥ karoti/
children.translated_text: Mars in the fifth causes calamity to sons; in the sixth, it quickly brings about the destruction of enemies.
In the seventh, loss of wealth, displeasure, disease, and torment; in the eighth, bondage, loss of wealth, disease, death, and fears.

children.text: dharmaṃ na sādhayati dharmagato mahījaḥ śasto 'mbare na śubhadaḥ kathito 'pariś ca/
children.translated_text: Mars in the ninth does not accomplish religious merit; in the tenth, it is praised but does not give auspiciousness; and some say it is without limit.

children.text: lābhe 'rthasiddhivibhavāgamadaḥ prayātur vittakṣayaṃ bahu karoti gataś ca riṣphe//
children.translated_text: In the eleventh, it gives success in purpose, authority, and income for the traveler; in the twelfth, it causes much loss of wealth.
Mercury in the ascendant brings fame, happiness, wealth, intelligence, and victory; in the second, it gives wealth;

children.text: sotkaṇṭhaṃ sa virāgameti sahaje kāmān labhetākhilān/
children.translated_text: in the third, it goes forth with longing and dispassion; in the fourth, one obtains all desires.
In the house (4th), bed, food, drink, and wealth; in the fifth, the arrival of a son;

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe yāty aribādhyatāṃ śaśisute kleśaś ca yātur bhavet//
children.translated_text: in the sixth, Mercury (son of the Moon) brings affliction from enemies and hardship for the traveler.
In the seventh (wife's house), Mercury gives attainment of excellent women, garments, and wealth; when fallen from the Sun [i.e., combust],

children.text: kecit kleśam uśanti naidhanagate śaṃsanti kecic chubham/
children.translated_text: some say there is hardship in the eighth; some declare it auspicious.

children.text: dharme dharmavivṛddhir ambaragate siddhir bhaved īpsitā
children.translated_text: In the ninth, increase of religious merit; in the tenth (mid-heaven), the desired success is achieved.

children.text: vidyārthāptir ayatnataś ca parato riṣphe ca vācyo vyayaḥ//
children.translated_text: Knowledge, attainment of wealth effortlessly, and after that; in the twelfth, expenditure is to be declared.

children.text: kīrtir lagne 'rthāthasiddhir dvitīye duścikyasthe kṣucchramārtiḥ surejye/
children.translated_text: Jupiter in the ascendant gives fame and success in purpose; in the second, it gives hunger, fatigue, and pain;

children.text: pātālasthe dharmatatvābhimānā kāryaṃ sidhyaty ātmajasthe 'py asādhyam//
children.translated_text: in the fourth, pride in religious truth; in the fifth (house of sons), the task succeeds though seemingly impossible.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe jīve śatrurāyāti vaśyaṃ kecit prāhur vaśyatāṃ yāti śatroḥ/
children.translated_text: Jupiter in the sixth brings the enemy under control; some say [the traveler] comes under the enemy's control.

children.text: vindanty aste 'riṣṭayoṣāyaśāṃsi mṛtyau prāṇān hanty athānye jagur na//
children.translated_text: In the seventh, one finds inauspicious women and ill-repute; in the eighth, some say it kills—others say it does not.

children.text: putrotpattir dharmasiddhiś ca dharme jīve karmaṇy arthasiddhir yaśaś ca/
children.translated_text: In the ninth, birth of a son and success in religious matters; Jupiter in the tenth brings success in purpose, wealth, and fame.

children.text: lābhe kāryaṃ vāñchitaṃ yāti siddhiḥ riṣphe prāpte kliśyate 'nekaduḥkhaiḥ//
children.translated_text: In the eleventh, the desired task reaches fulfillment; in the twelfth, one is afflicted by many sorrows.
Venus (<s>Bhṛgu</s>) in the ascendant [gives] attainment of courtesans, wealth, garments, garlands, food, and happiness;

children.text: lābho 'rthe sahaje na sīdati gataḥ prāpnoti śreṣṭhāṃ śrutim/
children.translated_text: in the second, gain; in the third, no distress—having gone, one attains excellent learning.
In the fourth, arrival of friends; in the fifth, attainment of position, wealth, and honor.
In the sixth, defeat of enemies, displeasure, and grief; when in the [seventh] place, they have declared otherwise.
Venus in the seventh, having given wife and wealth, cuts off one's own territory;
in the eighth, it accomplishes the task; in the ninth, it quickly achieves the desired [goal].
Venus in the tenth gives the traveler abundant wealth; in the eleventh, it gives victory and wealth.

children.text: vyarthaṃ dvādaśago vyayaṃ prakurute śasto 'parair dvādaśe//
children.translated_text: In the twelfth, it causes fruitless expenditure; some praise it in the twelfth.

children.text: bandhaṃ vadhaṃ cārkasute vilagne dhane arthahāniṃ labhate śubhaṃ ca/
children.translated_text: Saturn (<s>Arkasuta</s>) in the ascendant [causes] imprisonment and death; in the second, loss of wealth, though some good;

children.text: śatror balaṃ hanti gatas tṛtīye caturthago bandhubhayaṃ parebhyaḥ//
children.translated_text: in the third, it destroys the enemy's strength; in the fourth, fear from kinsmen and from others.

children.text: nārthasya siddhiḥ sutage 'rkaputre ripūn ripusthe sṛjayaty ayatnāt/
children.translated_text: In the fifth, no success in purpose; in the sixth, Saturn effortlessly defeats enemies.
In the seventh, loss of enthusiasm and eye disease; in the eighth, death by poison, fire, weapons, and the like.

children.text: dharme na dharmaṃ labhate sukhañ ca yānāvṛtiṃ karmaphalaṃ ca svasthe/
children.translated_text: In the ninth, no religious merit or happiness; in the tenth (own place), the fruit of work and obstruction of vehicles.

children.text: ekādaśasthe jayavittalābhān mande 'ntyage nārtham upaiti yātā//
children.translated_text: In the eleventh, victory, wealth, and gains; in the twelfth, Saturn does not bring wealth to the traveler.
Generally, planets placed in the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th [houses]
are [declared] malefic, [and those in] auspicious [houses] are benefic—excluding the son of the Sun (Saturn) in the 10th.
Benefics going everywhere produce auspicious results,
except when Jupiter (guru of the gods) is in the 7th, for one who desires conquest.
Some say that Venus, excluding the 6th, 12th, 7th, and 3rd houses,
is best; Mercury (son of the Moon) in the 12th, 9th, 3rd, and 7th is not otherwise;
the Moon is honored when in the 11th, 5th, 2nd, 9th, 3rd, and 10th;
Jupiter going everywhere is declared by <s>Maṇittha</s> [to be good], but not when in the 12th, 6th, and 7th.

children.text: ekīyapakṣe 'pi hi kaiścid ukto bhṛguḥ śubho 'ntyātmajalābhavarjam/
children.translated_text: In the view of some, Venus is also declared auspicious except in the 12th, 1st, 5th, and 11th;
the Moon in the 7th, 6th, 3rd, 8th, 10th, and 7th; Mercury in the 7th, 1st, 8th, 4th, and 12th.
Chapter 11: General Rules and Exceptions (<s>utsargāpavāda</s>)

children.text: saumyāsaumyeṣv etal lagnādstheṣu yat phalaṃ proktam/
children.translated_text: The results stated for [planets] stationed from the ascendant in benefic and malefic [houses]—
are not absolute, due to the variation of results when [multiple planets] transit simultaneously.

children.text: horāvido jagur idaṃ sutāv abalo daśādhipāriś ca/
children.translated_text: The astrologers have declared: the lord of the <s>daśā</s> (planetary period), if weak, a son, and enemies—
give inauspicious results when current; even a benefic in the ascendant does not give desired results.

children.text: sāmprataṃ śubhadaḥ sutau balanvito yo daśādhi(pa)mitraṃ ca/
children.translated_text: Conversely, the lord of the <s>daśā</s>, if endowed with strength, a son, and a friend—
even a malefic gives auspicious results; there is a verse taught in the <s>śāstra</s> on this:
Even a benefic that takes exceedingly long to produce results should not be employed;
even a malefic whose result is not current and who is conquered by enemies [should not be employed].
The lord of the <s>daśā</s>, purified through the <s>aṣṭakavarga</s> (eightfold division) of its own house, the 8th, etc.—
is not without result even if weak; and the same applies to the system of the day-lord's <s>aṃśa</s> (division).
Some teachers desire a benefic <s>daśā</s>-lord stationed in the ascendant,

children.text: pāpāṃ copacayasthaṃ na vilagne tatra ca ślokau//
children.translated_text: and a malefic in an <s>upacaya</s> (increasing) house, not in the ascendant; and on this there are two verses:
When benefic planets are in the ascendant, the result is certainly auspicious.
When a malefic planet rises, the result for the traveler is without doubt inauspicious.
Therefore, a malefic lord of the <s>daśā</s>, endowed with the traveler's valor and qualities,
should be placed in <s>upacaya</s> houses, never in the ascendant.

children.text: tac ca viruddhaṃ teṣāṃ katham anyadaśāsu dāsyate svaphalam/
children.translated_text: But that is contradictory—how will they give their own results in other <s>daśās</s>?

children.text: evaṃ phalasya nāśo vrajati sarvasya phalali(lī)psoḥ//
children.translated_text: Thus the destruction of results goes for one who desires all results.

children.text: tasmān naikānto 'yaṃ jātakam avalokya nirdiśet sadasat/
children.translated_text: Therefore this [rule] is not absolute; having examined the birth chart (<s>jātaka</s>), one should predict auspicious and inauspicious [results].

children.text: ślokau vṛttaṃ bhedaṃ prāha maṇittho vasiṣṭhaś ca//
children.translated_text: Two verses: <s>Maṇittha</s> and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> teach the distinction in practice:

children.text: rakṣakā vardhakāś caiva ye syur janmani nāyakāḥ/
children.translated_text: Those planets that are protectors, promoters, and rulers in the birth [chart]—

children.text: tān pāpān api niḥśaṅko yātrālagneṣu yojayet//
children.translated_text: them, even if malefic, one should without hesitation employ in the travel ascendant.
The auspicious and inauspicious yogas (combinations) that are stated in the birth chart—

children.text: tān sarvān avalokyaiva prayāṇeṣv api yojayet//
children.translated_text: having examined all of them, one should apply them to journeys as well.

children.text: horāgataḥ svabhavane yadi sūryaputro meṣopago 'vanisutaḥ svagṛhe śaśāṅkaḥ/
children.translated_text: If Saturn, come from the <s>horā</s>, is in its own house; if Mars is in <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) in its own house; the Moon,

children.text: śukras tulādharagato mithune budhaś ca siṃhe ravir yadi ca pārthivajanma vidyāt//
children.translated_text: Venus in <s>Tulā</s> (Libra), Mercury in <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini), and the Sun in <s>Siṃha</s> (Leo)—then one should know it as a royal birth.
Those planets that at the time of birth are situated in the Moon's rising and <s>upacaya</s> [houses]—

children.text: te sarve nānākhyā krūrāḥ saumyaiḥ samāścintyāḥ//
children.translated_text: all of them, though called malefic in various ways, should be considered together with the benefics.

children.text: yo yasya daśamagṛhagaḥ sa tasya vaśyas tu bhavati niyamena/
children.translated_text: Whichever [planet] occupies the tenth house of another—that one necessarily becomes subservient to the other.

children.text: yaś cātha paṇapharasthaḥ sa bhavati rakṣopagas tadvat//
children.translated_text: And whichever [planet] is situated in the sixth or twelfth house, that one is associated with <s>rakṣas</s> (demons), likewise.
Those that have gone to the <s>upacaya</s> (growth) houses are mutually to be declared as renowned, but unequal;
The significators mentioned earlier in the <s>Prakīrṇaka</s> (Miscellaneous) chapter [apply here too].

children.text: janmeśvaralagnapayor yaḥ śatrur lagnagaḥ sa saumyo 'pi/
children.translated_text: Whichever [planet] is an enemy of the lord of birth and the lord of the ascendant, even if benefic, when situated in the ascendant,

children.text: kurute dehavipattiṃ krūro 'pi śubhaṃ tayor mitram//
children.translated_text: Causes bodily misfortune; even a malefic that is a friend of those two produces good.

children.text: bhaven na yaḥ kārakatānasaṃjñaḥ svajanmalagnādhipayoḥ śubho 'pi/
children.translated_text: One who is not designated as a <s>kāraka</s> (significator) for one's own birth and ascendant lords, even if benefic,

children.text: karoti lagnopagataḥ sa yātur bhayaṃ vināśaṃ ca bahuprakāram//
children.translated_text: When placed in the ascendant, causes fear and manifold destruction for the traveler.
Even a malefic placed in the ascendant bestows good upon men if designated as <s>kāraka</s> (significator);

children.text: tasmāt praytnād idm eva cintyaṃ yiyāsatāṃ kārakatānayātam//
children.translated_text: Therefore, those who wish to travel should carefully consider the <s>kāraka</s> system of travel.

children.text: eko 'pi vakropagato narāṇāṃ śubho 'śubho vāpi catuṣṭayasthaḥ/
children.translated_text: Even a single [planet], whether benefic or malefic, when retrograde and situated in a <s>catuṣṭaya</s> (quadrant),
Or even a <s>varga</s> (division) of it rising at the ascendant, causes manifold destruction for travelers.
The Sun in its own or the fifth house, when in the ascendant, gives delight in women and jewels;
When situated in the remaining houses, it swiftly gives slaughter, bondage, and agitation.
The Moon, having reached the ascendant, when situated in any house for those setting forth,
Causes increase of enemies, loss of splendor, and obstruction.
Mars, in the house of Saturn, when in the ascendant, gives destruction of enemies and victory;
The son of Earth (Mars), when situated in the remaining houses, causes loss of jewels and wealth.
Mercury, when situated in the ascendant in the houses of the Sun, Moon, or Mars, gives misfortune;
In [the houses of] Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn, it brings consecration, victory, wealth, and splendor.
Jupiter in the house of Venus or the Moon is said to bring destruction of wealth and warriors;
In the remaining houses, it gives territory, allies, wealth, and victory to the friend of the earth (the king).
Venus in the house of Mercury, when in the ascendant, diminishes strength, gives wealth, and destroys enemies;
In the houses of the remaining [planets], it causes wind-fever and the anger of enemies.
Saturn in the house of the Sun, when in the ascendant, brings delight, happiness, and gain;
Undesirable when in other houses, it causes loss of power, strength, and honor.
The son of the Sun (Saturn) in its own house causes destruction of wealth and body;
The cold-rayed one (Moon) [brings] attainment of women and jewels, and sovereignty over kings; the Sun,
The son of the Earth (Mars) [brings] agitation of the army and hearing of pleasing [news]; Mercury,
The guru of the gods (Jupiter), when in a chariot, brings attainment of enjoyments; Venus gives victory.

children.text: yo 'staṃ yāty udayaṃ vā dakṣiṇamārgasthitaḥ sahastrāṃśoḥ/
children.translated_text: Whichever planet, situated on the southern path of the Sun, sets or rises
While in conjunction with the ascendant, causes loss of warriors, wealth, and body for the traveler.

children.text: tigmakarasyottarato darśanam āyāti yo graho 'staṃ vā/
children.translated_text: A planet that appears north of the Sun, or that sets,

children.text: madhye tu vā sa lagne yātuḥ kusumāmbarāśanadaḥ//
children.translated_text: Or [is] in the middle — when in the ascendant, it gives flowers, garments, and food to the traveler.
An anomaly in the fixed course, brilliance, color, or size [of a planet] is called a <s>vikṛti</s> (aberration);

children.text: vikṛtistho galnagato na śubhaḥ śubhadaḥ svabhavanasthaḥ//
children.translated_text: One in a state of aberration when in the ascendant is not auspicious; one in its own house is auspicious.

children.text: yāmye tamo jñaḥ śravaṇe ravis tu jāto viśākhāsu sitaś ca puṣye/
children.translated_text: Mercury is born in <s>Yamya</s> (Bharaṇī), the Moon in <s>Śravaṇa</s>, the Sun in <s>Viśākhā</s>, Venus in <s>Puṣya</s>,
In <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (Revatī), <s>Abhijit</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, and <s>Kṛttikā</s> are born Saturn, Mars, Rāhu, and the Moon-born (Mercury) [respectively].
The <s>nakṣatra</s> that is strongly struck by the three kinds of portents and afflicted by planets —
When it falls in the ascendant during a military expedition, it should be avoided even if otherwise favorable.
When the friend or neutral of the lords of the <s>pāka</s> (planetary period) and the ascendant, or their <s>varga</s> (division), is in the ascendant of the traveler,

children.text: svayam arir upaiti vaśyaṃ praṇataśirāḥ sārvabhaumo 'pi//
children.translated_text: The enemy himself comes under submission — even a universal sovereign with bowed head.

children.text: pakeśvarārilagne varge vā tasya bhūpatir gacchan/
children.translated_text: When the enemy of the lord of the <s>pāka</s> [is] in the ascendant, or its <s>varga</s>, the king who marches
With his heroes and horses slain, comes under the enemy's submission.
Body, wealth, warriors, vehicles, ministers, enemy, path, resources, mind,
Profession, income, and expenditure — these are declared as the significations beginning from the ascendant.

children.text: yātrāphalaṃ caturthe jāmitre śatravaḥ pramādaś ca/
children.translated_text: The result of the expedition [is seen] in the fourth; enemies and negligence in the seventh;
One should predict the auspicious and inauspicious of these from the conjunction of benefic and malefic planets.

children.text: satyācāryasya mate vibalaḥ śastaḥ śaśī prayāṇeṣu/
children.translated_text: In the view of the teacher <s>Satya</s>, the Moon is recommended when weak for departures;

children.text: digvīryonaḥ kevalam induḥ śasta iti jagur anye//
children.translated_text: Others say that only the Moon devoid of directional strength is recommended, merely lacking directional vigor.

children.text: yad eva yasyodayasaṃsthitasya phalaṃ prayāṇe sadasat pradiṣṭam/
children.translated_text: Whatever result — good or bad — is declared for a planet situated at the ascendant during departure,

children.text: tad eva tasyākhilam ahni yātur grahasya varge ca vilagnasaṃsthe//E38
children.translated_text: That entire [result] applies to the traveler on that day when that planet or its <s>varga</s> is situated at the ascendant.
Chapter 12: <s>Miśraka</s> (Miscellaneous).

children.text: vyasanaṃ prāpno(ti) mahad vyatipāte nirgato 'thavā mṛtyum/
children.translated_text: One who departs during <s>Vyatīpāta</s> encounters great calamity or death;
The same [applies] when traveling during <s>Vaidhṛti</s>; they prescribe the same for the three-day contact period.
One should not travel on the night of the new moon; there is fault in that; on an intercalary month there is calamity;
A king seeking victory should not set forth at the juncture of a season, an <s>ayana</s> (solstice), or a <s>yuga</s>.
The friends, neutrals, and enemies arising from the <s>varga</s> portions of the lords of one's own <s>nakṣatra</s> and planetary period,
Are likewise declared as the friends, neutrals, and enemies of the one seeking conquest who experiences that period.
An enemy [whose period is] void and inauspicious should certainly be exterminated by the one seeking conquest;
One whose period is descending should be oppressed; one whose [period] is ascending should likewise be worn down.

children.text: na sadṛśadaśo 'bhiyojyaḥ sandhānaṃ tena bhūpater vyāsam/
children.translated_text: One with an equal period should not be attacked; the king should make a treaty with him;
