One whose approaching period is inauspicious should make a treaty with one whose approaching period is auspicious.
War is preferable in the reverse situation — when the period is ascending and the approaching period inauspicious —
When the enemy is situated far away during an auspicious approaching period.
A king with an ascending period, an auspicious approaching period, and the period-lord endowed with strength,
Should march; the opposite [situation warrants] a dual policy; a mixed period [calls for] ambivalent [action].
During a period afflicted by voidness, and when the enemy [has] the period of the lord of birth and ascendant,
A king whose own period-lord is the <s>kāraka</s> period-lord should seek refuge.

children.text: upacayakartur vrajed diśaṃ balavati kaṇṭakage ca dikpatau/
children.translated_text: One should march in the direction of the planet that makes growth [houses], and when the lord of the direction is strong in the <s>kaṇṭaka</s> (angular) [position];

children.text: manasāpi na digbalānvite digadhipatau ca lalāṭasaṃsthite//
children.translated_text: Not even in thought [should one march] in a direction whose directional lord is weak and whose directional lord is situated at the forehead [i.e., the tenth house].
The lords of birth and ascendant, when endowed with strength and situated in growth and angular houses, give auspicious results;

children.text: krūrāv api nityam eva tau saumyair eva samāv udāhṛtau//
children.translated_text: Even if malefic, those two are always declared as equivalent to benefics.
The lords of one's own period, birth, and ascendant, when conjoined with the twilight sun, are inauspicious;
Except for Venus and Saturn — those emerging from the Sun are middling.

children.text: parasparaṃ saurikujau ravīndū trikoṇagau bhārgavalohitau ca/
children.translated_text: Saturn and Mars mutually, the Sun and Moon mutually, Venus and Mars mutually, when in trine —

children.text: phalaṃ yad uktaṃ tad aśeṣam eva vināśya paścāt svadiśaṃ nayantām//
children.translated_text: Whatever result has been declared, all of it is destroyed; afterward they lead [the traveler] to his own direction.

children.text: ripudivaso yasya bhavet saumyo 'pi sa lagnago na śubhadātā/
children.translated_text: A planet whose day is that of the enemy — even if benefic, when in the ascendant it does not give good;
Even a malefic generates the desired result when it is a friend, on its own day, situated in the ascendant.
The lords of the year, month, day, and <s>horā</s> (hour), when strong and placed in angular positions,
Give doubly auspicious or inauspicious results; beyond these, other planets [are less significant] for the traveler.
When the ascendant is in [the signs of] Leo, Sagittarius, or Aries, the expedition is superior; in the houses of Saturn, Mercury, and Venus it is middling;

children.text: bhānau kulīrajhaṣavṛścikage 'tidīrghā śastas tu devalamate 'dhvani pṛṣṭhato 'rkaḥ//
children.translated_text: When the Sun is in Cancer, Pisces, or Scorpio, it is very long; but according to teacher <s>Devala</s>, the Sun behind [the traveler] is recommended for the journey.
When endowed with a <s>daśā</s> (period) that gives full results, the expedition is excellent; middling when purified by the <s>aṣṭavarga</s>;
Of lesser results [are those determined] by the momentary ascendant, <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), day-lord, <s>karaṇa</s>, and so forth.
The expedition of highest result [occurs when] benefics are in trines, exaltation, and growth [houses];
Middling when in their own or friendly houses; lowest when in depression, enemy, and [the sixth] house.
Middling-lowest-lowest, highest-equal-middling, lowest-lowest-highest-superior,
And middling-highest as the sixth — these are the expedition [grades] desired by those versed in expedition [astrology].
When the Moon is in a retrograde [sign in the] directional <s>varga</s>, afflicted, or conjoined with the twilight Sun,

children.text: śukre pravasan narer vaśaṃ yāti budhe ca vilomasaṃsthite//
children.translated_text: And Venus — when setting forth, the man comes under [the enemy's] control; likewise when Mercury is in retrograde position.

children.text: anulo(ma)gate śaśāṅkaje śukre caivam api vyavasthite/
children.translated_text: When Mercury and Venus are in direct motion, and likewise situated,
One should march without apprehension; Jupiter is described by others as having the same [effect] as Mercury.

children.text: ākrandasārī dinamadhyago 'rkaḥ pauraḥ purastād aparatra yāyī/
children.translated_text: The Sun at midday is an <s>ākranda</s> (cry for help) [planet and] a <s>sārī</s> (traveler); a <s>paura</s> (citizen) in front; otherwise a <s>yāyī</s> (marcher);

children.text: ākranda indur gurumandasaumyāḥ paurāḥ smṛtā yāyina ity ato 'nye//
children.translated_text: The Moon is <s>ākranda</s>; Jupiter, Saturn, and Mercury are <s>pauras</s> (citizens); the rest are declared as <s>yāyins</s> (marchers).
With <s>yāyī</s> (marching) planets endowed with strength and victory, some declare the enemy's expedition auspicious;

children.text: satyaṃ tathā kiṃ tu viśeṣam āhus te bhūpateḥ satphaladā jigīṣoḥ//
children.translated_text: True, it is so; but they state a distinction — they give true results for a conquering king.

children.text: dṛṣṭe sāmnāṃ karmaniṣṭaṃ surārau vaitālīyaṃ pādadambhau ca hitvā/
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāhu</s> is seen, pacification rites are best; abandoning the <s>Vaitālīya</s> [meter rites] and foot-deceptions,

children.text: śasto rāhus tryāyakarmopayāto yātavyaś cāsannatāgaś ca ketuḥ//
children.translated_text: <s>Rāhu</s> is recommended when employed in the three-fold ritual; and <s>Ketu</s>, when approaching, should be traversed.

children.text: sāmnāṃ śukrabṛhaspatī dinakaro vakraś ca daṇḍeśvarau
children.translated_text: Venus and Jupiter are [the planets] of pacification; the Sun and Mars (retrograde) are the lords of punishment;
The Moon, <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, and Saturn are of dissension; the nocturnal planet (Moon) is of conciliation through gifts.
From the Sun [comes] forest warfare; from <s>Yama</s> (Saturn), [warfare with] hired forces; from Venus, [warfare with] guild [forces];
From Mercury, [warfare through] spells; the enemy-land, local forces, and protector [forces come from] Mars, Moon, and Jupiter respectively.
The king should march in the direction from which the lord of the day and the lord of the <s>nakṣatra</s> have been displaced, for the purpose of destroying the enemy's treasury;

children.text: athāyanena yugapad ekasaṃsthayor dyunaktayo raviśaśinor vrajet tadā//E25
children.translated_text: But when the [lords of] day and night, the Sun and Moon, are together in one [sign], one should march by income [strategy] at that time.
Chapter 13: <s>Dehaspandana</s> (Body Tremors).
I shall describe the tremor of the right side [of the body]; on the left side it indicates the opposite result;
On the head, gain of territory; on the forehead, increase of position.
Between the eyebrows and nose, meeting with a beloved; at the eyes, acquisition of servants;
At the outer corner of the eye, gain of wealth; in the eastern [part], restless longing is to be known.

children.text: yoṣitsaukhyaṃ gaṇḍe dṛkcaramādhaś ca saṅgare vijayaḥ/
children.translated_text: On the cheek, pleasure from women; below the outer corner of the eye, victory in battle;

children.text: śravaṇe ca hitaśravaṇaṃ nāsāyāṃ prītisaukhyaṃ ca//
children.translated_text: At the ear, hearing of beneficial [news]; at the nose, delight and happiness.
At the lower and upper lips, meeting with a beloved and victory; at the throat, attainment of enjoyments;
At the shoulder, increase of enjoyments; union with one mounted on a vehicle.

children.text: haste 'rthāptiḥ pṛṣṭhe parājayo vakṣasi smṛto vijayaḥ/
children.translated_text: On the hand, gain of wealth; on the back, defeat; on the chest, victory is declared;

children.text: prītyutpattiḥ pārśve stane tv apūrvā viṣayalabdhiḥ//
children.translated_text: On the side, arising of delight; on the breast, unprecedented acquisition of territories.
On the hip, joy from strength; at the navel, declared loss of position;
On the hand, increase of treasury; at the heart, distress ending in wealth.
On the buttock, gain of a vehicle; on the testicle, longevity; on the penis, arrival of a woman;
On the scrotum, birth of a son; on the bladder, prosperity of the inner quarters.

children.text: pṛṣṭhata ūrvor doṣaḥ purataś calane tu śacivahitalabdhiḥ/
children.translated_text: On the back of the thighs, harm; but when the front trembles, gain of chariot-mounted allies;

children.text: pracalati ca jānusandhāv arisandhānaṃ balavad uktam//
children.translated_text: When the knee-joint trembles, a powerful alliance with the enemy is declared.
On the shin, destruction of a part of the territory; on the upper ankle, gain of position;
When the sole of the foot trembles, a journey [and] loss.
Wounds, boils, moles, marks, and fly-bites and such are to be interpreted [similarly];
Itching on the right palm of the king leads to victory.
Chapter 14: <s>Cittaśuddhi</s> (Purity of Mind).
The king should be asked confidently in private by the astrologer:

children.text: ripunidhanapraṇidhānaṃ prati bhavataḥ kiṃ manaḥ kurute//
children.translated_text: "What does your mind incline toward regarding the plan to destroy and suppress the enemy?"

children.text: brūyāt sa cen mama manaḥ protsahate harṣayet tataś caivam/
children.translated_text: If he should say, "My mind is eager and enthusiastic," then [the astrologer] should encourage him thus:
"The favorableness of the mind is the mark of success." And on this there are verses:
All omens, auspicious and inauspicious, may be on one side;

children.text: ekataś ca manaśśuddhis tad dhi śuddhaṃ jayāvaham//
children.translated_text: And purity of mind on the other — for that which is pure brings victory.

children.text: kiyac ciraṃ na labhyeta nimittaṃ gamanānugam/
children.translated_text: How long may one fail to obtain an omen favorable to the march?

children.text: na tv eva tu mano 'narthaṃ cireṇāpy anumanyate//
children.translated_text: But the mind never consents to misfortune, even after a long time.
Following the omens, subtle, greater than the body and the senses,

children.text: tejo hy etac charīrasthaṃ trikālaphaladaṃ nṛṇām//
children.translated_text: This radiance dwelling in the body gives results of the three times to men.
The mind does not delight in misfortunes, nor does it rejoice in failure;

children.text: tasmāt sarvātmanā yātur anumeyaṃ sadā manaḥ//E6
children.translated_text: Therefore, the mind of the traveler should always be carefully observed.
Chapter 15: <s>Guhyakānuṣṭhāna</s> (Rites for the <s>Guhyakas</s>).
Seven days before the expedition, for three days [perform] the rite of alliance with the <s>Guhyakas</s> (secret beings); then

children.text: tryaham atha vijayasnānaṃ gṛhayajñaṃ saptame divase//
children.translated_text: For three days the victory-bath; on the seventh day, the domestic sacrifice.
With cooked and raw meat, curds, fruits, flowers, liquor, rice-pudding, and offerings in return;
With radish-food, fragrances, incense primarily of <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium);
Attended by the royal astrologer, minister, chief priest, trusted men, and armed attendants,
He should go to the crossroads of the city, wearing fresh garments and an upper cloth over his body.

children.text: ardhaniśāyām udayati saumye vakre 'thavā tadaṃśe vā/
children.translated_text: At midnight, when a benefic [planet] rises, or when retrograde, or in its <s>aṃśa</s> (division),

children.text: dadyād baliṃ daśasv apy āśāsu purohitaḥ kramaśaḥ//
children.translated_text: The chief priest should offer <s>bali</s> (oblations) in all ten directions, in order.
The priest, with palms joined, should there recite the <s>Rudra-Sāvitrī</s> [hymn],
And then chant the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, <s>Mahārauhinaka</s>, and <s>Kubera-hṛdaya</s> [hymns].
Those dwelling at gates, at crossroads, at quadrangles, on mountains, in cities, and in gardens;
Those dwelling on highways, riverbanks, in caves, and in crevasses;
Of manifold forms, great beings, great souls, of great vows —
O foremost ones, accept this offering; homage be to you!
"This king, with good sons, ministers, and servants, together with his wife,
He should be protected, and you should strive for his welfare with concentrated minds.

children.text: evam uktvā tatas tv arghyaṃ pramathebhyaḥ pradāpayet/
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he should then offer the <s>arghya</s> (respectful offering) to the <s>pramathas</s> (attendants of Śiva).
On that consecrated ground of <s>Sāvitrī</s>, the charioteer should present the offering.
To <s>Yama</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Artheśa</s> (Kubera), <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Pāvaka</s> (Fire), and the Trident-bearer (<s>Śiva</s>),
to <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, and <s>asuras</s> likewise,

children.text: ye syur bhūtagaṇās tebhyo namo 'stv ity anuyāntu ca/
children.translated_text: whatever hosts of spirits there may be — "Homage to them!" they should say, and let them follow.
Armed with their weapons, slayers of the enemy army,
let them follow behind, accompanied by the army, adorned with varied garlands and ornaments, intoxicated with frenzy,
wearing varied garments, matted-haired, crowned, with terrifying, pot-bellied, hunchbacked, and dwarfish [forms].

children.text: nivṛttayātraḥ punar apy ahaṃ hi vo vijitya śatrūn bhavatāṃ prasādataḥ/
children.translated_text: "Upon my return from the campaign, having conquered the enemies by your grace,

children.text: ato viśiṣṭaṃ bahuvittam uttamaṃ baliṃ kariṣye vidhinopapāditam//
children.translated_text: I shall perform for you an offering even more distinguished, abundant in wealth, supreme, prepared according to the proper rite."

children.text: anarcitā ye nṛpatiṃ savāhanaṃ vināśayanti kṣapayanti vā camūn/
children.translated_text: Those [spirits] who are not worshipped destroy the king together with his vehicles, or diminish his armies;

children.text: supūjitāḥ siddhikarā bhavanti te pravādhakāḥ śatrugaṇasya cāhave//
children.translated_text: but when well-worshipped, they become bestowers of success and destroyers of the hosts of enemies in battle.
For the duration of merely one-sixtieth of a <s>kṣaṇa</s> (moment), the king, having purified himself, should dismiss the <s>pramathas</s>.
Then, with auspicious rites announced by the astrologer and the royal priest, he should depart.
Chapter 16: Dreams.
The king, wearing silk, pearls, and jewels, accompanied by his minister, astrologer, and royal priest,
should enter his own deity's temple and there install the images of the guardians of the directions.

children.text: abhyarcya mantrais tu purohitas tān adhaś ca tasyāṃ bhuvi saṃskṛtāyām/
children.translated_text: The royal priest, having worshipped them with <s>mantras</s>, should then on that consecrated ground below,

children.text: darbhais tu kṛtvāstaram akṣatais ca kiret samantāt sitasarṣapaiś ca//
children.translated_text: make a bed of <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) and <s>kuśa</s> grass, and scatter unbroken rice grains and white mustard seeds all around.

children.text: brāhmīṃ sadūrvām atha nāgapuṣpīṃ kṛtvopadhānaṃ śirasi kṣitīśaḥ/
children.translated_text: The lord of the earth, having made a pillow of <s>brāhmī</s> (herb) with <s>dūrvā</s> grass and <s>nāgapuṣpī</s> (serpent-flower) at his head,

children.text: pūrṇān ghaṭān puṣpaphalābhidhānān āśāsu kuryāc caturaḥ krameṇa//
children.translated_text: should place full pots covered with flowers and fruits in the four directions in order.

children.text: yaj jāgrato dūram upaiti daivam āvartya mantrāṃ kramaśas trir etam/
children.translated_text: That which divine fate reaches far while one is awake — having recited this <s>mantra</s> three times in sequence,

children.text: laghv ekabhug dakṣiṇapārśvaśāyī svapnaṃ parīkṣeta yathopadeśam//
children.translated_text: eating lightly once, lying on the right side, one should examine the dream according to the instruction.
Homage to <s>Śambhu</s>, the Three-Eyed, to <s>Rudra</s>, the Supreme Self,
to the Dwarf, to the Deformed One, homage to the Lord of Dreams!
O Blessed One, God, Lord of Gods, Trident-bearer, Bull-rider,
reveal to me, while sleeping in a dream, that which is auspicious and inauspicious, eternally.
Wearing a single garment, having slept on a bed of <s>kuśa</s> grass, with a purified mind,

children.text: niśānte paśyati svapnaṃ śubhaṃ vā yadi vā 'śubham//
children.translated_text: at the end of the night one sees a dream, whether auspicious or inauspicious.

children.text: gataiṣyajātyantarasattvasaṅgaiḥ svapne 'py anūke gatije ca nityam/
children.translated_text: By associations with beings of past, future, and intervening births, in dreams too, the habitual tendencies of past and present are constant.
Due to the agitation of the wind-natured [humor] of the traveler, [one dreams of] leaping over mountains, high ridges, and the sky.
When bile predominates, one sees gold, jewels, garlands, the sun, fire, and the like.
When phlegm predominates, [one dreams of] the moon, radiance, white flowers, crossing rivers, lakes, and oceans.
In the last, middle, and first watches of the night, and in the seasons called rainy, autumn, and spring,
the results are general, arising from the agitation of wind, bile, and phlegm [respectively]; a combined result occurs when [all humors are] concurrent.

children.text: daśāsu coktaṃ grahapākajātaṃ cintā tu dṛṣā tu yathā tathaiva/
children.translated_text: The results arising from planetary periods are stated in the ten [chapters on] planetary periods; those from deliberation [are as stated], and those actually seen are likewise.
Terrifying dreams, being overcome by spirits, sorcery — these are declared to arise from <s>guhyakas</s> (hidden beings), [indicating] the arising of obstacles.
Those [dreams] arising from habitual tendencies, deliberation, planetary afflictions, or things actually seen, as well as those from past <s>karma</s>, are fruitless.

children.text: dyudṛṣṭapūrvāḥ kathitāś ca tadvad anyatra loke kathitā viśeṣāḥ//
children.translated_text: Those seen during the day or previously, and those narrated — likewise; but those narrated otherwise in the world are [considered] special.
That [dream] which is as vivid as direct perception and seems to flash from within —
from such a dream, the attainment of good or bad results is certain.
Dreams, whether auspicious or inauspicious, are fruit-bearing for humans;
I shall describe them here in summary.
One's own body blazing, ascending to a high place, embracing <s>Indra</s>'s banner,
the earth turning around, flinging the body of a king's daughter in the directions,

children.text: bandho vā nigale grasec ca dahanaṃ nānāśirobāhutā
children.translated_text: being bound in chains, fire swallowing [one], having many heads and arms,

children.text: chatraṃ vā dvirado 'bhiṣicya bibhṛyād divyo 'thavā brāhmaṇaḥ//
children.translated_text: or a parasol, an elephant consecrating and bearing [one], or a divine <s>brāhmaṇa</s> —
being anointed with water flowing from the tips of stars', sun's, or cow's horns,
or the pleasant milking of a she-buffalo, a lioness, a tigress, or cows,
wrapping intestines emerging from the belly around village trees and the like,

children.text: viśati yadi vā suśliṣṭāṅgī tanuṃ pravarāṅganā//
children.translated_text: or a beautiful woman of fine limbs entering one's body —
eating of human hearts and heads, or eating the flesh of one's own body,
of serpents, horses, lions, elephants, and goats —
or the sprouting of grass, trees, flowers, and water from one's own navel,
or the overturning and uprooting of the earth's surface — [these portend] sovereignty.
Eating, touching the sun, moon, and stars,

children.text: daraṇam api ca mūrdhnaḥ sapta pañca tridhā vā/
children.translated_text: and also the splitting of the head into seven, five, or three parts,
mounting a bull, a house, a lordly elephant, a horse, an elephant, or a lion,
swallowing the ocean and the earth — these are signs that grant sovereignty.
Conquering in great battles, contests of destruction, gambling, and debates,
obtaining cattle, deer, or human beings, or the highest seat,
eating excrement, being smeared [with it], or going to a forbidden woman,
one's own death, obtaining a funeral pyre, and the sight of a harvest —
seeing white, fragrant, and pleasing ointments, garlands, and garments,
seeing <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, gods, the <s>guru</s>, and kings, and receiving blessings,
eating curd or fine rice in vessels of jewels, silver, gold, or lotus-shaped [vessels],
or immersion in blood —
obtaining a white horse, a chariot, a banner, a parasol, a fan, a lotus, a jewel, or a lordly elephant,

children.text: abhaya jaya ca bhuṃkṣva ceti śabdāḥ pariṇatarājyaphalapradāḥ pradiṣṭāḥ//
children.translated_text: and the words 'Fear not!', 'Victory!', and 'Eat!' — these are declared to bestow the fruit of accomplished sovereignty.
The movement in the form of beings practiced in former births,

children.text: (tada)nūkam iti proktam iha paścāt karoti yat//
children.translated_text: that is called 'habitual tendency'; what one does afterward in this [life] —
in [dreams of] seals and the like, sacrificial threads, and signs of women, the obtaining of a woman is indicated.
In obtaining a bed, or a mirror, or a ewer and the like, the birth of a son [is indicated].

children.text: kāminyāṃ dhanalabdhir ambutaraṇe śokasya nāśo bhaved
children.translated_text: In [a dream of] a woman of desire, the obtaining of wealth; in crossing water, the destruction of grief;

children.text: dharṣo roditaśocitādiṣu tathā dāhe vivṛddhir matā/
children.translated_text: outrage is [indicated] in weeping, lamenting, and the like; in [dreams of] fire, increase is considered [the result].
Whatever cows, horned animals, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, deities, ancestors, friends, and kings declare

children.text: svapne tan niyamād bhavaty avitathaṃ neṣṭaṃ śubhaṃ vā phalam//
children.translated_text: in a dream, that invariably comes true — whether undesirable or auspicious in its fruit.
In [dreams of a] cow or bear, or another lineage, the sprouting of grass, trees, and flowers, drinking oil,
play, riding, and enjoyment; and in [dreams of] beings of the form of donkeys, monkeys, camels, serpents, and the like —
or the smearing of the body with turbid, impure, ink, cow-dung, oil, or mud,
or the falling off of eyes, tongue, teeth, or arms — these are signs portending misfortune and grief.
Singing, sports, being adorned, laughing, being delighted, and playing,
the falling of the sun, moon, banner, or stars, and going along a river —
the cutting of a rope, a funeral pyre, falling into a precipice, entering the mother's body,
and the grinding of bronze in a dream and [injury to] the head — these give affliction, disease, and misfortune.
Growing of beard, hair, and nails in length, worshipping an ugly woman or a monkey-woman,
wearing red garments and kneading human limbs — these portend disease, death, fear, grief, and suffering.
The floating in a mass of water of land animals, cattle, insects, aquatic creatures, and the blind,
or a wedding festival,
playing with lotuses, lac, or pots, or dancing,
being unclothed and filthy — these quickly portend disease.

children.text: svadravyanāśaḥ suhṛdāṃ viyogaśchedaś ca pāṇyoḥ kamalāpahāraḥ/
children.translated_text: Loss of one's own property, separation from friends, cutting of the hands, theft of lotuses,
descending from palaces, houses, or mountain-peaks — in dreams these are declared inauspicious.

children.text: mitrasyāptiḥ syādvikośāsilābhe vaśyaṃ gacched bhūpateḥ śāsanāptau/
children.translated_text: Obtaining a friend is [indicated] in [dreams of] obtaining a scabbard or a whetstone; submission is [indicated] upon receiving the king's order.

children.text: sarpe karṇau nāsikāṃ vā praviṣṭe tacchedaḥ syād veṣṭane cāśu bandhaḥ//
children.translated_text: When a serpent enters the ears or nose, cutting of those [organs] results; and when [the serpent] coils around, swift bondage [results].

children.text: ādye varṣād vatsarārdhād dvitīye yāme pāko varṣapādāt tṛtīye/
children.translated_text: In the first watch of night, the result manifests within a year; in the second watch, within half a year;

children.text: māsāt pākaḥ śarvarīpaścimāṃśe sadyaḥ pāko govisarge ca dṛṣṭe//
children.translated_text: in the third watch, within a quarter of a year; in the last portion of the night, the result is immediate; and [what is seen] at the time of releasing the cows [i.e., dawn].

children.text: dṛṣṭvā svapnaṃ śobhanaṃ neha supyāt paścād dṛṣṭo yaḥ sa pākaṃ vidhatte/
children.translated_text: Having seen an auspicious dream, one should not sleep again afterward; a dream seen afterward [i.e., after re-sleeping] brings its result.

children.text: śaṃsediṣṭaṃ tatra sādhudvijebhyas te tvāśibhiḥ pūjayeyur narendram//
children.translated_text: One should declare the auspicious [dream] to virtuous <s>brāhmaṇas</s> there; they should honor the king with blessings.

children.text: bhūyaḥ prasvapanaṃ na cāsya kathanaṃ gaṅgābhiṣeko japaḥ
children.translated_text: No sleeping again, and no telling [the dream to others]; bathing in <s>Gaṅgā</s> water, recitation,
pacificatory rites, well-wishing ceremonies, and also the morning attendance upon a cow and an <s>aśvattha</s> (fig) tree,
worship of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with sesame, food, drink, and flowers according to one's ability,
meritorious acts and the recitation of the <s>Bhārata</s> (Mahābhārata) — these are prescribed for the removal of bad dreams.
Chapter 17: The Victory Bath.
Places for bathing should be: trees with milky sap, the ocean, cotton plants, river confluences, a lake, or a dry [riverbed],
a cow-station, a level place, a gods' temple, or a beautiful spot.
On even, deep, non-saline, grassy ground, with water flowing to the right,
one should draw a <s>vāstu</s> (ritual ground plan), <s>sarvato bhadra</s> (auspicious in all directions), measured by a stick's shadow.
With all grains — sesame, green gram, black gram, chickpea, and flax interspersed,
strewn all around with <s>darbha</s> and <s>kuśa</s> grass with unbroken tips.
With pots containing silver, jewels, and gold inside, along with milk, coral, and white threads,
and with dark roots — adorning the gateway, in the middle of that [enclosure].

children.text: tanmadhye brāhmī brahmā sāma dūrvāgraśaṃkhapuṣpāḥ syuḥ/
children.translated_text: In the middle [should be placed]: the <s>brāhmī</s> [plant], a [figure of] <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, tips of <s>dūrvā</s> grass, and conch-flowers.
Facing the direction, of the height of an arm's length, it should be placed, full and with an enclosure.

children.text: tasya grahānulomaṃ kālaṃ kecij jagur niṣeveta/
children.translated_text: Some say the time should follow the sequence of planets; the ritual priest should serve that [time].
The offering ... and the meal of sixty-day [matured] barley-rice and milk-porridge.
With mind devoted to his chosen deity, the king should enter through the eastern gate.
Having sat on the auspicious seat in a clockwise direction, then the ritual proceeds.
With <s>priyaṅgu</s> (beauty-berry), white mustard, <s>nāgadāna</s>, <s>gorocanā</s> (ox-gallstone pigment), and <s>akṣa</s> (beads) mixed with clarified butter,
self-protection should first be performed with objects purified against counter-spells, for the king who is about to bathe.

children.text: śvetasya babhror athavā vṛṣasya carmāstare vyāghramṛgendrayor vā/
children.translated_text: On a hide spread out — of a white or tawny bull, or of a tiger or lord of beasts (lion) —

children.text: tatsthasya kuryān manujeśvarasya jayābhiṣekaṃ vidhivat purodhāḥ//
children.translated_text: the royal priest should perform the victory-consecration in the proper manner for the lord of men standing upon it.

children.text: kramān mahīrūpyasuvarṇakumbhaiḥ kṣīrasya dadhno haviṣaś ca pūrṇaiḥ/
children.translated_text: In sequence, with pots of earth, silver, and gold filled with milk, curd, and clarified butter,

children.text: snāyāc ca toyaiḥ saha saptamṛdbhiḥ paścāc ca sarvauṣadhigandhatoyaiḥ//
children.translated_text: he should bathe with waters together with the seven earths, and afterward with waters infused with all herbs and fragrances.
Having consecrated [the waters] with the <s>Mahārauhiṇaka</s>, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, <s>Kuverahṛdaya</s>, and <s>Rudragaṇa</s> [mantras],
the royal priest should consecrate the king with prosperity.

children.text: dvātriṃśatiṃ ṣoḍaśa vāthavāṣṭau ghaṭapramāṇaṃ munibhiḥ pradiṣṭam/
children.translated_text: Thirty-two, or sixteen, or eight — this is the measure of pots prescribed by the sages.

children.text: snātas tv alaṅkāram apāsya pūrvaṃ navaṃ vidadhyād dvijamantrapūrtam//
children.translated_text: Having bathed, one should set aside the former ornaments and put on new ones, consecrated with <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>mantras</s>.
With auspicious and well-wishing words spoken by <s>Māgadha</s> bards, friends, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and charioteers,
the consecrated [king] should sit on the hides of a spotted deer, a lordly elephant, a cat, and a wolf.
Holding incense, garments, garlands, and fragrance, having circled the herbs three times over him,

children.text: vāme 'sya pārśve 'grata āsthito vā pratīpapātaṃ juhuyād dhutāśam//
children.translated_text: standing on his left side or in front, one should offer oblations into the fire in the reverse direction.
After applying <s>gorocanā</s>, gold, fruits, clarified butter, <s>brāhmī</s> with <s>dūrvā</s> grass, and white mustard seeds,

children.text: āsevya sarvāṇi yathopadeśaṃ bhaktyā dvijān svasti ca vācayitvā//
children.translated_text: and performing all [rites] as instructed, having worshipped the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with devotion and had them recite blessings,

children.text: saumyena yāyāt phalapuṣpapāṇir dvāreṇa paśyen na ca pauruhūtam/
children.translated_text: the king should depart through the northern gate, carrying fruits and flowers in hand, and should not look at the eastern direction.

children.text: prāg uddhared dakṣiṇapādam evaṃ kurvan nṛpaḥ sarvaripūn praśāsti//E16
children.translated_text: He should first raise his right foot — the king who does thus subdues all enemies.
Chapter 18: Planetary Sacrifices.

children.text: grahayajñam ato vakṣye tatra nimittāni lakṣayed vedyām/[cited in bs 43.14]
children.translated_text: I shall now describe the planetary sacrifice. One should observe the omens there at the altar.
A break in the altar line [portends] loss of honor; if displaced from its direction, failure [of the rite].
It causes the destruction of the city-priest, queen, general, or king,
in the eastern, southern, western, northern, and central portions respectively, wherever it is defective.
There the image for the Sun should be made of copper, the ladle of <s>palāśa</s> (sacred fig) wood, and the fuel-sticks likewise.

children.text: ā kṛṣṇeti ca mantro raktā gandhāḥ sahāguraṇāḥ//
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is 'ā kṛṣṇa...' etc.; the fragrances should be red, accompanied by <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood).
The food should exclude black gram, flax, sesame, sunflower, and chickpea;
and the worship with flowers of <s>vakula</s>, <s>arka</s> (calotropis), <s>agastya</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, and <s>śallakī</s> (frankincense).
To eight hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who maintain the sacred fires, the offering-fee should be given,
consisting of a bull, gold, and land, dedicating it to the Thousand-rayed One (the Sun).

children.text: nyagrodhāt sruksamidhaḥ sphaṭikād arcā ca śitagoḥ kāryā/
children.translated_text: For the Moon, the ladle and fuel-sticks should be of banyan wood, the image of crystal, and the [offerings] of a white cow.
The fragrances should exclude <s>śaileya</s> (rock moss) and <s>nakha</s> (nail-shaped spice); the flowers should be white.
Wheat, <s>śāli</s> rice, barley, and <s>vaṇḍa</s> (pulse) with cow's milk as the first food; then the <s>mantra</s>,
'<s>āpyāyasva</s>...' etc., and the offering should be given to one learned in the four <s>Vedas</s>.
One should offer a cow endowed with gems, pearls, silk garments, and gold, white in color with a matching calf,

children.text: rajataśaphaviṣāṇāṃ kṣīriṇīṃ ca tu himāṃśum uddiśya//(candraḥ)
children.translated_text: with silver-plated hooves and horns, and yielding milk, dedicated to <s>Himāṃśu</s> (the Moon). (<s>Candraḥ</s>)

children.text: raktakaravīrasamidho raktā gandhāś ca candanāt pratimā/
children.translated_text: The <s>samidh</s> (sacrificial fuel) should be of red <s>karavīra</s> (oleander), the fragrances should be red, and the image should be made from sandalwood.
The <s>mantra</s> is 'Agnir mūrdha' (Agni is the head); the food offering should consist mainly of <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> (quick-ripening rice).
Copper, gold, coral, and woolen garments should be given as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee),
dedicated to <s>Dharātanaya</s> (the Son of the Earth, i.e., Mars), to <s>Chandoga</s> (Sāmaveda) priests who are observing vows. (<s>Maṅgalaḥ</s>)
The <s>mantra</s> is 'Udbūdhyasva' (Awake!) and so forth; the image should be made of mixed metals.

children.text: sruksamidhaś ca madhūkād atha vā cāndrer apāmārgāt//
children.translated_text: The <s>sruk</s> (sacrificial ladle) and <s>samidh</s> (fuel-sticks) should be of <s>madhūka</s> (mahua), or else of <s>apāmārga</s> (prickly chaff-flower) as prescribed for the Moon.
The fragrances should consist mainly of mixed substances such as <s>kālīyaka</s> (dark sandalwood), <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), <s>priyaṅgu</s> (beauty-berry), and the like.
The flowers should be <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine), <s>vakula</s> (bullet-wood), <s>tilaka</s> (sesame flower), <s>madayantikā</s> (henna), and so forth.
The food offering should be lentils, sesame, <s>śāli</s> (rice), <s>mudga</s> (mung beans), <s>caṇaka</s> (chickpeas), and the like; the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) should be a pure
gem set in silver, given to ascetics observing vows and to <s>Ātharvana</s> (Atharvaveda) priests, as prescribed for the Moon. (<s>Budhaḥ</s>)
The <s>samidh</s> (fuel-sticks) should be of <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) and <s>arjuna</s> (terminalia) trees; the image should be of gold; the fragrances should exclude fire-based ones.
The flowers for <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) should be yellow; the food offering should be sesame, <s>mudga</s> (mung beans), and <s>caṇaka</s> (chickpeas).
One should give to <s>Bahvṛca</s> (Ṛgveda) priests a horse of a single color, of middle age,
equipped with a horn ornament and gold. The <s>mantra</s> of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) is 'Bṛhaspateś ca.' (<s>Bṛhaspatiḥ</s>)
The image for <s>Bhṛgusūnu</s> (Venus, son of Bhṛgu) should be of silver; the fragrances should be aphrodisiac; the flowers should be variegated and fragrant.
The <s>samidh</s> (fuel-sticks) should be of <s>panasa</s> (jackfruit) and <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig); the food offering should be aphrodisiac.

children.text: annāt parisrutādyo mantraḥ strīkarkaśās tv alaṅkārāḥ/
children.translated_text: From food and <s>parisrut</s> (fermented liquor) and the like; the <s>mantra</s> should be of feminine intensity; the ornaments
should be given to thirty-two <s>Adhvaryu</s> (Yajurveda) priests who are worthy of such gifts. (<s>Śukraḥ</s>)

The <s>sruk</s> (ladle) and <s>samidh</s> (fuel-sticks) should be of <s>śāla</s> (sal) and <s>śamī</s> (prosopis); the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Bhāskara</s>'s son (Saturn) is 'Śaṃ no devī' (May the goddess be auspicious to us).
The image should be of iron; the fragrances should be <s>śaileya</s> (rock lichen), <s>mustaka</s> (cyperus), and <s>śukti</s> (conch-shell powder) predominantly.
The flowers should be black ones such as <s>girikarṇikā</s> (glory lily), <s>tasī</s> (flax), <s>spandana</s> (trembling plant), <s>añjana</s> (collyrium plant), and the like.
The food offerings should consist chiefly of black sesame, <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), <s>caṇaka</s> (chickpeas), and <s>niṣpāva</s> (flat beans).
One should give a female servant past her prime, equipped with tin, collyrium, lead, and iron,
dedicated to <s>Ārki</s> (Saturn, son of the Sun), to low-caste men, husbands of <s>vṛṣalī</s> women, the aged, and the foolish. (<s>Śaniḥ</s>)
The <s>sruk</s> (ladle) and <s>samidh</s> (fuel-sticks) for <s>Rāhu</s>'s <s>homa</s> (fire oblation) should be of <s>vaibhīta</s> (Meyna laxiflora), or alternatively <s>dūrvā</s> (bent grass).

children.text: mantraś ca kayā naścitrapūrvako 'rcā ca nāgamayī//
children.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> is 'Kayā naścitra' preceded by its initial syllables; the image should be made in the form of a serpent.
Dedicated to <s>Saiṃhikeya</s> (Rāhu, son of Siṃhikā), one should bestow a buffalo upon well-respected

children.text: viprebhya iti yad anyat tat sarvaṃ sūryaputrasamam//(rāhuḥ)
children.translated_text: Brahmins. Whatever else remains is all the same as for the son of the Sun (Saturn). (<s>Rāhuḥ</s>)

children.text: ketoḥ kāṃsyapratimā ketuṃ kṛṇvann na ketave mantraḥ/
children.translated_text: For <s>Ketu</s>, the image should be of bronze; the <s>mantra</s> for <s>Ketu</s> is 'Ketuṃ kṛṇvann' (Making the banner).
The worship should be with wild forest flowers; the <s>sruk</s> (ladle) and <s>samidh</s> (fuel-sticks) should be of <s>khadira</s> (catechu) and <s>kuśa</s> (sacred grass).
The food offering is <s>māṃsaudana</s> (meat-rice); the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) should be given to the family of the <s>brahmabandhu</s> (nominal Brahmins),
along with weapons and miscellaneous items — thus dedicated to <s>Ketu</s>. (<s>Ketuḥ</s>)
Chapter 19: <s>Agnilakṣaṇa</s> (Characteristics of Fire)

children.text: kṛtvaivaṃ grahapūjām ṛcā tataś cāgniliṅgayā juhuyāt/
children.translated_text: Having thus performed the planetary worship, one should then make oblations with the <s>ṛc</s> (Vedic verse) pertaining to the characteristics of fire.
I shall now recite the verses on this subject as taught by the sage <s>Kāśyapa</s>.

children.text: tato 'pratirathaṃ kṛtsnaṃ yātrāliṅgaṃ ca yad bhavet/
children.translated_text: Then one should recite the entire <s>Apratiratha</s> (Invincible) hymn, and whatever constitutes the omen-hymn for the march,
and the <s>Āyuṣya</s> (Life-giving) hymn, the <s>Abhaya</s> (Fearlessness) hymn, and the entire <s>Aparājita</s> (Unconquered) hymn.
Also the group of <s>Śarman</s> and <s>Varman</s> hymns, and likewise the group of <s>Svastyayana</s> (benedictory) hymns.
Having offered these five groups of hymns into the fire and having established the sacred fire according to proper rites,

children.text: bhūta bhūteti ca gaṇaṃ yatte candras tathaiva ca/
children.translated_text: one should also recite the 'Bhūta bhūta' group, and the 'Yat te Candra' group likewise,

children.text: aindro gaṇas tathā cāndro mantrāśīḥsūktam eva ca//
children.translated_text: and the <s>Aindra</s> (Indra) group and the <s>Cāndra</s> (Moon) group, and the <s>Mantrāśīḥsūkta</s> (hymn of mantra-blessings).

children.text: bhūyo bhūyas tathā jvālāṃ saṃspṛśyātha purohitaḥ/
children.translated_text: Again and again touching the flame, the <s>purohita</s> (royal priest)

children.text: spṛśec ca nṛpatiṃ mantrair uccair brūyāt punaḥ punaḥ//
children.translated_text: should touch the king with <s>mantras</s> and proclaim aloud repeatedly:

children.text: cakṣurdaḥ prāṇadaś cāpi varcodaś ca bhava prabho/
children.translated_text: "Be a giver of sight, a giver of breath, and a giver of vigor, O Lord!
You are most inviolable, just as you, O <s>Havyavāhana</s> (fire, carrier of oblations), are."

children.text: śātravāṇāṃ tathā rājāpy anādhṛṣyo bhavaty ayam/
children.translated_text: "Thus may this king also become inviolable to his enemies."

children.text: hūyamāne nimittāni vakṣyāmy aham ataḥ param//
children.translated_text: I shall now describe the omens that appear while the oblation is being offered.
Trembling, coughing, yawning, shaking, sweating, shedding tears, hunger,

children.text: dgārādyaṃ ca purodhasaḥ smṛtivipac cāniṣṭam anyac chubham/
children.translated_text: belching, and the like in the <s>purohita</s> (priest), as well as loss of memory, are inauspicious; other things are auspicious.
Clarified butter contaminated with hair, ants, or impurities, or that which has been licked by animals —

children.text: tan neṣṭaṃ śubham anyathopakaraṇaṃ dravyāṇy anūnāni ca//
children.translated_text: that is inauspicious; otherwise the implements are auspicious, provided the ritual substances are complete and undiminished.

children.text: utthāya svayam ujjvalārcir analaḥ svāhāvasāne havir
children.translated_text: If the fire rises on its own with a blazing flame, if at the conclusion of the <s>svāhā</s> invocation it consumes the oblation,

children.text: bhukte dehasukhaḥ pradakṣiṇagatiḥ snigdho mahān saṃhataḥ/
children.translated_text: if it is comfortable in form, moves clockwise, is smooth, great, and compact,
if it is smokeless, fragrant, free of sparks, favorable to the direction of march, gentle,
and bearing the luster of pearls, blue lotuses, and gold — it foretells victory for the marcher.
If the fire takes the shape of auspicious objects — a pot, a parasol, a horse, a <s>Śrīvṛkṣa</s> (holy tree), or a mountain —
and its sound resembles that of a drum, ocean, kettledrum, or a smooth-sounding cart, it is honored.
The opposite of what has been described is inauspicious; however, a smooth fire is always auspicious.

children.text: savye 'ṅge nṛpatiṃ dahann atihitaḥ śeṣaṃ ca lokād vadet//E10
children.translated_text: If it burns the king on the left side of the body, it is extremely beneficial; the rest one should determine from common observation.
Chapter 20: <s>Prasthānika</s> (The Departure Ceremony)

children.text: vrajed digīśaṃ hṛdaye niveśya yathendra mainryām aparāś ca tadvat/
children.translated_text: The king should set forth, having placed the guardian deity of the direction in his heart — <s>Indra</s> for the east, <s>Maināka</s> for other directions likewise — wearing pure white garlands and garments, and should step forward with his right foot first.
Under a white parasol, resplendent with gems and jewels, fanned by white <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisks),
with the royal highway filled with cries of victory, his splendor enhanced by the <s>mantras</s> of the foremost Brahmins,
stationed amidst maidens, ministers, trusted attendants, warriors,
astrologers, Brahmins, and chamberlains,

children.text: dvātriṃśataṃ samupagamya padāni bhūmau prāgādi nāgarathavājinraiḥ prayāyāt//E3
children.translated_text: having walked thirty-two steps on the ground, he should then proceed forward with elephants, chariots, horses, and foot soldiers.
Chapter 21: <s>Gajalakṣaṇa</s> (Characteristics and Omens of Elephants)
Lest there be excessive length here due to digression on the characteristics of elephants, horses, and men,
I shall describe only the essentials of omens relevant to the time of departure for kings.
Those elephants with copper-colored lips, palate, and mouth, with eyes like the <s>kalaviṅka</s> (sparrow) bird, with smooth and prominent front teeth, with broad and elongated faces,
with arched, elongated, deep-set, and concealed spinal columns, with fine single hairs and forehead bosses resembling the tortoise,

children.text: vistīrṇakarṇahanunābhilalāṭaguhyāḥ kūrmonnatair\footnote{Bṣ 66.7b kūrmonnata-} dvinavaviṃśatibhir nakhaiś ca/
children.translated_text: with broad ears, jaws, navel, forehead, and private parts, with twenty-nine nails raised like a tortoise's back,
with round trunks adorned with three lines, with trumpeting like the rumbling of rain-laden clouds,
with long toes and reddish trunk-tips, with trumpeting like the rumbling of rain-laden clouds,
with large, long, and round necks — such elephants of the king are considered auspicious.
Those without <s>mada</s> (ichor), with excessive, deficient, or deformed nails and limbs, hump-backed, dwarfish, with ram-like or twisted horns,
lacking visible sheaths, testicles, or trunk-tips, with tawny, dark blue, piebald, or white palates,
with scanty facial hair, infested with bugs, broken-tusked, as well as a female elephant bearing the marks of a male elephant,

children.text: garbhiṇīṃ ca nṛpatiḥ paradeśaṃ prāpayed ativirūpaphalās te//
children.translated_text: and a pregnant one — the king should send these to foreign lands, for they yield extremely ugly results.
One should determine the length of the tusk by twice the circumference at its root, and then prepare it beyond that.
A tusk that appears tawny, putrid, impure, or reddish, resembling a creature of evil nature, yields evil results.

children.text: pārthivopakaraṇākṛtiṃ yadā cihnam udvahati kalpite rade/
children.translated_text: When a carved tusk bears a mark in the shape of a royal insignia,
then there will be increase of prosperity, victory, purpose, and strength; smooth, white, and lustrous ones are auspicious.

children.text: dakṣiṇe śubham atīva śobhanaṃ pāpam apy ativirūpam anyataḥ/
children.translated_text: On the right side, an omen is exceedingly auspicious and beautiful; on the other side, even an auspicious sign yields extremely ugly results.
In the reverse case, the result is moderate; further elaboration has been declared by other sages.
At the root, middle, and tip of the tusks are situated <s>Devas</s> (gods), <s>Daityas</s> (demons), and <s>Manujas</s> (humans) respectively; accordingly,
the result is abundant at the middle, diminishing at the ends; it manifests quickly at the middle and slowly at the extremities.
The result of a tusk breaking on the right side causes loss of territory, army, and rout.
On the left, it destroys the prince, the <s>purohita</s> (priest), the army commander, forest chieftains, wives, and generals.
From observing breakage on both sides, one should predict the complete destruction of the king's lineage.
With auspicious <s>lagna</s> (ascendant), <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), and the like, the good result increases; otherwise the inauspicious prevails.
When the left or middle tusk breaks or chips against milk-bearing trees, fruit trees, flowering trees,
or by collision against riverbanks, it destroys the enemy; otherwise the reverse.

children.text: skhalitagatir akasmāt trastakarṇo 'tidīnaḥ śvasiti mṛdu sudīrghaṃ nyastahastaḥ pṛthivyām/
children.translated_text: An elephant that stumbles in its gait, with suddenly frightened ears, extremely distressed, breathing softly and deeply, with its trunk placed on the ground,

children.text: drutamukulitadṛṣṭiḥ svapnaśīlo vilomo bhayakṛd ahitabhakṣī naikaśo 'sṛcchakṛtkṛt//
children.translated_text: with rapidly half-closed eyes, drowsy, moving in reverse — it causes fear; eating inauspicious food, repeatedly discharging blood and dung,
destroying anthills, tree stumps, bushes, grass, and trees, looking about at will,

children.text: yāyād yātrānulomaṃ tvaritapadagatir vaktram unnāmya coccaiḥ/
children.translated_text: proceeding in the direction of the march with swift steps, raising its face and trumpeting aloud,

children.text: kakṣāsannāhakāle janayati ca muhuḥ śīkaraṃ vṛṃhitaṃ vā
children.translated_text: and at the time of girding and harnessing, repeatedly producing a spray of <s>mada</s> (ichor) or trumpeting,

children.text: tatkālaṃ vā madāptir jayakṛd atha radaṃ veṣṭayan dakṣiṇaṃ ca//E15
children.translated_text: or obtaining <s>mada</s> (rut) at that very time — this foretells victory; and likewise wrapping its right tusk.
Chapter 22: <s>Vājilakṣaṇa</s> (Characteristics and Omens of Horses)
Horses endowed with qualities of <s>āvarta</s> (whorls), spirit, luster, color, breed, gait, voice, and bodily features
bring victory to kings — in brief. Here follows a partial instruction on <s>āvartas</s> (hair whorls).
<s>Āvartas</s> (whorls) on the tear-ducts, jaw, cheek, heart, throat, nostrils, conch of the ear, hip, bladder, knee,
scrotum, navel, hump, anus, left flank, and feet are inauspicious.
Those <s>āvartas</s> (whorls) situated on the water-trough area, throat, ears, middle of the back, above the eyes,
lips, hock-joint, shoulder, flank, and sides — these, together with the forehead, are very auspicious.
The tail-hair, rays of hair, neighing, smoke, and flame and such signs should be observed at the time of exertion in horses.
Here the <s>āryā</s> verses composed by <s>Viṣṇugupta</s> are declared.
Among these, fire appearing at the rear part of the saddle or its back portion during release
is inauspicious; elsewhere it is favorable; the same applies to the left and right flanks.
Equally, fire, burning sparks, and smoke on the feet, mane, and tail
cause national calamity, disease, panic, and crushing defeat by the enemy's forces.

children.text: prākphalatulyaṃ pṛṣṭhe jaghane vāleṣu caiva nirdiṣṭam/
children.translated_text: On the back and haunches, the result is the same as stated before; and likewise on the tail hairs.
Fire on the penis, whether with smoke or without, indicates revolt in the inner palace.
And always when the tail-hair is aflame, burning, flame, sparks, and smoke
on the shoulder, saddle, and upper arm region portend slaughter and captivity in battle.
When horses are neighing and flame arises from the chest, eyes, forehead, and shoulders, as well as from their mouths,
the generation of flame grants victory; the generation of smoke portends the destruction of the master.
On the nostrils, tear-ducts, muzzle, head, and eyes, at night,
blazing of tawny, dark, green, and piebald colored horses portends victory.

children.text: vijayāya sarvaidaiva hi suśuklaśukavarṇayor jvalanam eṣu/
children.translated_text: Blazing of pure white and parrot-green colored horses in all these places invariably portends victory.

children.text: evaṃ ca yathāsambhavam anyeṣv api vāhaneṣu phalam//
children.translated_text: And thus, the results apply as appropriate to other mounts as well.
Henceforth, one should carefully observe neighing as indicative of auspicious or inauspicious results.
Neighing produced with an outstretched and steady neck yields auspicious results.
When horses neigh loudly with food in their mouths, in a smooth, resonant, and deep tone,
and are honored with Brahmins, full vessels, auspicious substances, garlands, fragrances, and wine-root offerings,
and are gratified with bridle, food, drink, armor, and the master's accoutrements,
it conduces to the accomplishment of all purposes, especially when they look toward the right side.
At the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight) junctures, horses that are blazing, facing a cardinal direction, agitated, deeply restless, and sleepless,
neighing — they cause fear and bring about slaughter, captivity, and defeat.
Those with curled tails, lying on the right side, are inauspicious.
Those striking the ground with their left hooves should be understood as portending a long absence.

children.text: sajṛmbhaṇaṃ pṛṣṭhavidhūnanaṃ ca vālaprakāras tv asakṛl lilikṣoḥ/
children.translated_text: Yawning, shaking the back, repeatedly spreading the tail as if wishing to lick,
and touching one foot with another — these are signs of horses that foresee the mobilization of the army.
Horses with sleepless, sluggish, dark-blue eyes, lost in deep thought with vacant memory during the day,

children.text: niśāsu cānyonyavirodhanaṣṭanidrās turaṅgā na śivāya bhartuḥ//
children.translated_text: and sleepless at night due to mutual hostility — they do not bode well for the master.

children.text: jaṃghe liṃhannavraṇaromapaṅke pādau ca saṃhṛṣṭatanur jayāya/
children.translated_text: One licking its shank, a wound, or matted hair, and stamping its feet with bristling body — this portends victory.

children.text: viparyayaḥ paścimayoḥ prayatnāt svayaṃ tu yātrābhimukho niyamya//
children.translated_text: The reverse for the hind legs; but if it spontaneously faces the direction of march and restrains itself, that too portends victory.

children.text: muhurmuhur mūtraśakṛt karoti na tāḍyāmāno 'py anulomayāyī/
children.translated_text: One that repeatedly passes urine and dung, that does not follow the proper course even when struck,

children.text: akāryabhīto 'śruvilocanaś ca śivaṃ na bhartus turago vidhatte//
children.translated_text: that is frightened of its duty and sheds tears from its eyes — such a horse does not bring welfare to the master.

children.text: ārohati kṣitipatau vinayopapanno yātrānugo 'nyaturagaṃ pratiheṣitaś ca/
children.translated_text: When the king mounts, a horse that is well-trained, follows the direction of march, and neighs in response to another horse

children.text: vaktreṇa vā spṛśati dakṣiṇam ātmapārśvaṃ yo 'śvaḥ sa bhartur acirāt pratanoti lakṣmīm//E21
children.translated_text: A horse that touches the right side of its master with its mouth will soon bestow prosperity upon him.
Chapter 23: Auspicious and Inauspicious Omens (<s>śakunaśubhāśubha</s>)

children.text: anyajanmāntarakṛtaṃ puṃsāṃ karma\footnote{Bṣ 85.5b karma puṃsāṃ} śubhāśubham/
children.translated_text: The good and bad <s>karma</s> of people, performed in previous births,

children.text: yat tasya śukunaḥ pākaṃ nivedayati gacchatām//
children.translated_text: an omen-bird (<s>śakuna</s>) announces its ripening to those who are setting out on a journey.
Domestic, wild, aquatic, terrestrial, and aerial; moving by day, by night, or both—
in their calls, movements, sightings, and utterances, they should be classified as male, female, and neuter.

children.text: pṛthagjāty anavasthānād eṣāṃ vyaktir na labhyate\footnote{Bṣ 85.7d lakṣyate}/
children.translated_text: Due to the instability of individual species among these, their identification is not easily obtained.
For the purpose of describing general characteristics, [here are] two verses composed by the sages:
Those with plump, elevated, and elongated limbs, with broad necks and chests,
with few but deep calls—these are males, with firm gait.
Those with slender necks, heads, and noses, with delicate mouths, feet, and gait,
speaking pleasantly and softly—these are females; anything else is neuter.
Whether [a creature is] domestic, wild, etc.—one should ascertain from common knowledge.
Wishing to summarize, I speak only for the purpose of [military] travel.

children.text: pathyātmānaṃ nṛpaṃ sainye pure coddiśya devatām/
children.translated_text: For the traveler himself, [the omen indicates] the king; in the army, the city; and with reference to the deity,

children.text: sārthe prdhānaṃ sāmye tu\footnote{Bṣ 85.11d syāj} jātividyāvayodhikam//
children.translated_text: in a caravan, the leader; and when equal [in status], the one superior in caste, learning, or age.
In the directions of the freed, attained, approaching, and solar [quarters], the result is accordingly;
those [directions] are blazing, smoky, and calm, and the others after them.

children.text: tatpañcamadiśāṃ tulyaṃ phalaṃ\footnote{Bṣ 85.13b śubhaṃ} traikālyam ādiśet/
children.translated_text: The result for the fifth direction from that should be declared equal; [one should predict] results for three time periods.
For the remaining directions, the auspicious or inauspicious result should be declared according to proximity.
From [creatures] that are near and on low ground, the result comes quickly; from those elevated and distant, slowly.

children.text: sthānavṛdhyupaghātāś ca tadvad brūyāt phalaṃ budhaḥ\footnote{Bṣ 85.14d punaḥ}//
children.translated_text: The wise person should likewise declare the result regarding position, increase, and harm.
By the <s>kṣaṇa</s> (moment), <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism), wind, and Sun, [an omen is] divinely blazing, in ascending order;
[it is] blazing through action by its movement, position, state, voice, and behavior.
Thus tenfold: even a calm [omen], if benign, eating grass or fruit,
[is auspicious]; one eating meat or impure things is fierce; one eating grain is mixed.
Those situated in mansions, palaces, auspicious, and pleasant places
are excellent; also [those] on trees bearing sweet sap, milk-sap, fruits, and flowers.
At the proper time, those on mountains and in water are strong; day-movers and night-movers [are strong at their proper times].
Neuter, female, and male [creatures] are increasingly strong, in that order.
Endowed with strength through speed, species, power, position, joy, and courage,

children.text: svabhūmāv anulomāś ca tadūnāḥ syur vivarjitāḥ//
children.translated_text: and moving in their own territory in the natural direction—those lacking these are to be disregarded.
The rooster, elephant[-shrike], <s>cirillī</s> (a bird), the peacock, <s>vañjula</s> (wagtail), and <s>chikkara</s> (a bird),

children.text: balinaḥ siṃhanādāś ca kūṭapūrī ca pūrvataḥ//
children.translated_text: and those with powerful lion-like calls, and the <s>kūṭapūrī</s> (a bird)—these are [assigned to] the east.
The jackal, owl, <s>hārīta</s> (green pigeon), crow, <s>kokarkṣa</s> (a bird), and the <s>piṅgala</s> (tawny [bird]),
the pigeon, crying, wailing, and cruel sounds—these are [assigned to] the south.
The cow, hare, <s>krauñca</s> (crane), <s>lomāśa</s> (hairy [creature]), goose, <s>utkrośa</s> (osprey), and <s>kapiñjala</s> (francolin),
the cat, festive music, instrumental music, singing, and laughter—these are [assigned to] the west.
The <s>śatapatra</s> (woodpecker), deer, mouse, deer, single-hoofed animals, and the cuckoo,
the <s>cāṣa</s> (blue jay), porcupine, auspicious cries, bell-sounds, and conch-sounds—these are [assigned to] the north.
A domestic [creature] should not be regarded when in the wild, nor a wild one when in a village;

children.text: divācaro na śarvaryāṃ na ca naktaṃcaro divā//
children.translated_text: a day-mover should not [be regarded] at night, nor a night-mover by day.
Those paired [in mating], diseased, afflicted, frightened, quarreling, seeking prey,

children.text: āpagāntaritā mattā na grāhyāḥ śakunāḥ kvacit//
children.translated_text: separated by a river, or intoxicated—these omen-creatures should never be regarded.
The <s>rohita</s> (a deer), horse, goat, <s>vāleya</s> (a creature), deer, camel, antelope, and hare
are to be known as fruitless in winter (<s>śiśira</s>); in spring, the crow and the cuckoo.

children.text: na tu bhrādrapade grāhyāḥ sūkarāś ca\footnote{Bṣ 85.27b sva} vṛkādaya/
children.translated_text: In <s>Bhādrapada</s> (August-September), boars, wolves, and the like should not be regarded;
in autumn, aquatic [birds], cows, and cranes; in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> (July-August), the elephant and the <s>cātaka</s> (rain-bird).
Tigers, bears, monkeys, leopards, and buffalo, together with lizards—

children.text: hemante niṣphalā jñeyā bālāḥ sarve vimānuṣāḥ//
children.translated_text: are to be known as fruitless in the cold season (<s>hemanta</s>); all young [animals are fruitless], as are those without human [association].
Between the directions of <s>Indra</s> (east) and <s>Agni</s> (southeast), in three divisions, are situated
the treasurer, the fire-priest, and the priest for livelihood and water-rites—in clockwise order.
An artisan, a mendicant, a naked woman—between the south and the southeast;
and after that, those associated with elephant-keepers, cowherds, and religious practitioners.
Between the southwest and the west, [there are] women, charioteers, and thieves;
a spearman, a bird-augur, and a violent person—between the northwest and the west.
After that, those knowledgeable in poisons, slaughter, cattle-keeping, and deception;

children.text: dhanavānīkṣaṇīkaś ca mālākāras tataḥ param\footnote{Bṣ 85.23d paraṃ tataḥ}//
children.translated_text: a wealthy person, an inspector, and a garland-maker after that.

children.text: vaiṣṇavaś carakaś caiva vājinām rakṣaṇe rataḥ/
children.translated_text: A <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> devotee, a wandering ascetic, and one devoted to the protection of horses—
thus thirty-two divisions arise from the [eight] directions beginning with the east.

children.text: rājā kumāro netā ca dūtaḥ śreṣṭhī caro dvijaḥ/
children.translated_text: A king, a prince, a commander, an envoy, a chief merchant, a spy, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,
and an elephant-keeper—these are [assigned] from the east onward; <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and others in the four directions.

children.text: gacchatas tiṣṭhato vāpi diśi yasyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ/
children.translated_text: Whether the [traveler] is going or standing, in whichever direction
an omen-bird cries out, one should declare an encounter with a person of that direction.
Broken, terrible, piteous, harsh, intolerable, and decrepit
voices are inauspicious; auspicious are those that are calm, joyful, natural, and full.
The <s>śivā</s> (jackal), <s>śyāmā</s> (dark bird), <s>aralā</s> (a bird), <s>ucchupiṅgalā</s> (a tawny bird), and the house-lizard,
the sow, and the cuckoo—these are of male naming and [indicate omens] from the left.
Those of female naming are the <s>bhāsa</s> (vulture), <s>bhaṣaka</s> (barker), monkey, <s>śrīkarṇa</s> (a bird), and <s>chitkara</s>,
the peacock, <s>śrīkaṇṭha</s> (a bird), ant, <s>ruru</s> (a deer), and hawk—these are [omens] from the right.
Exclamations, clapping, auspicious cries, singing, conch-sounds, and water-sounds,

children.text: satūryādhvayanāḥ puṃvat strīvad anyā giraḥ śubhāḥ//
children.translated_text: with drums and chanting—[these are] auspicious like male [omens]; other words are auspicious like female [omens].

children.text: grāmyau madhyamaṣaḍjau tu gāndhāraś ceti śobhanāḥ/
children.translated_text: The domestic [notes], the middle <s>ṣaḍja</s>, and <s>gāndhāra</s>—these are auspicious;
<s>ṣaḍja</s>, middle, <s>gāndhāra</s>, and <s>ṛṣabha</s>—these are the beneficial musical notes.
In call, mention, and sighting, the lark (<s>bhāradvāja</s>), the goat, and the peacock
are auspicious; the mongoose and the blue jay are auspicious; the chameleon in front is inauspicious.
The mention of the <s>jāhaka</s> (a bird), snake, hare, boar, and monitor lizard is auspicious.
The call and sighting [of these] is inauspicious; the opposite holds for the monkey and the bear.
The odd-[numbered creatures] from the right are praised; deer, mongooses, and egg-born [birds are the same].
<s>Bhṛgu</s> (Venus/the sage) declared that the blue jay and the mongoose from the left [are auspicious], in the afternoon.

children.text: chitkaraḥ\footnote{Bṣ 85.44a chikkaraḥ} kūṭapūrī ca pirilī(?) cāhni dakṣiṇāḥ/
children.translated_text: The <s>chitkara</s>, <s>kūṭapūrī</s>, and <s>pirilī</s> (?)—in daytime, from the right;
those with fangs, together with lizards, are always praised from the left.

children.text: śreṣṭhe hayasite prācyāṃ śavamāṃse ca dakṣiṇe/
children.translated_text: In the east, the best [omen is] a horse's neighing; in the south, corpse-flesh;
in the west, roots and curdled milk; in the north, cows, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and holy men.
Web-footed and hoofed [creatures] are inauspicious from the east; from the south, weapon-strikers;
from the west, liquor and eunuchs; from the north, threshing-floors, seats, and ploughs.
In work, assembly, battle, entering, and lost-path [situations],

children.text: yānavyatyastagā grāhyā viśeṣaś cātra kathyate\footnote{Bṣ 85.47d vakṣyate}//
children.translated_text: the transposition of the vehicle [i.e., reversed rules] should be taken; and the distinction here will be explained.
By day, the deer, <s>ruru</s>, and monkey should be taken as [valid omens] like [those at] departure;
and in the first part of the day, the blue jay, wagtail, and rooster.
In the last part of the night, the <s>naptṛ</s> (a bird), <s>kokūka</s> (a bird), and tawny [owl];

children.text: sarva eva viparyasthā grāhyāḥ sārtheṣu yoṣitām//
children.translated_text: all [rules] are reversed for women's caravans.
For an audience with a king, [omens] should be taken as for departure, and also for entering.
For entering mountains and forests, and for fording rivers [the same applies].

children.text: vāmadakṣiṇagau śastau yau tu tāv agrapṛṣṭhagau/
children.translated_text: One from the left and one from the right are praised; but those same two, from the front and from behind,
when blazing through action, [portend] destruction for the traveler—these are called <s>praigha</s> (obstructors).
But those same two, each in its proper position, calm in call and behavior,
are omen-birds called <s>śakunadvāra</s> (omen-gate), [portending] success in one's purpose.

children.text: kecit tu śakunadvāram icchanty ubhayataḥ sthitaiḥ/
children.translated_text: Some, however, desire the omen-gate to be [formed] by birds of the same species stationed on both sides,
calm in behavior and call.

children.text: visarjayati yady eka ekaś ca pratiṣedhati/
children.translated_text: If one [bird] releases [i.e., signals departure] and another obstructs,

children.text: sa virodho 'śubho yātur grāhyo vā balavattaraḥ//
children.translated_text: that conflict is inauspicious for the traveler; or the stronger one should be heeded.

children.text: pūrvaṃ prāveśiko bhūtvā punaḥ prāsthāniko bhavet/
children.translated_text: If [a bird] first acts as an entering-omen and then becomes a departure-omen,
it foretells success with ease; upon entering, the reverse.

children.text: visṛjya śakunaḥ pūrvaṃ sa eva niruṇaddhi cet/
children.translated_text: If an omen-bird first releases [the traveler] and then the same one obstructs,

children.text: prāha yātur arer mṛtyuṃ samaraṃ\footnote{Bṣ 85.56d ḍamaraṃ} rogam eva ca//
children.translated_text: it foretells for the traveler the death of an enemy, a battle, or disease.
But omen-birds from the left, when blazing, announce danger.

children.text: ārambhe śakuno dīpto vṛṣānte\footnote{Bṣ 85.57d varṣāntas} tadbhayaṃkaraḥ//
children.translated_text: A blazing omen at the beginning [of a journey], at the end of the [sign of] <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), causes that [same] danger.
Blazing by <s>tithi</s>, wind, Sun, asterism, and position, behavior, and action—in that order,
they portend danger to wealth, army, strength, limbs, desired [goal], and undertakings.
When blazing at the sound of thunder-clouds, there is danger from wind;
those blazing at both twilights portend danger arising from weapons.
On funeral pyres, with hair and skulls, they give death, imprisonment, and slaughter;
on thorns, wood, and ashes, they give quarrel, fatigue, and suffering.
Stationed on worthless stones, blazing omen-birds cause failure or fear;

children.text: kurvanti śakunā dīptāḥ śāntā yāpyaphalās tu te//
children.translated_text: when calm, they produce tolerable [or neutral] results.
Those that bring success or failure should be known as [respectively] the one that carries away and the one that brings food.

children.text: sthānāt krośan\footnote{Bṣ 85.62c ruvan} vrajed yātrāṃ śaṃsate tv anyathāgamam//
children.translated_text: One that cries from its perch and then departs announces a journey; otherwise, a return.
When blazing in voice, quarrel; when blazing in position, conflict.

children.text: uccam ādau dhvaniṃ\footnote{Bṣ 85.63c svaraṃ} kṛtvā nīcaṃ paścāc ca doṣakṛt//
children.translated_text: Making a loud sound first and then a low one afterwards is fault-producing.

children.text: ekasthāne ruvan dīptaḥ saptāhād grāmanāśakṛt\footnote{Bṣ grāmaghātakaḥ}/
children.translated_text: One that cries blazing from a single spot causes the destruction of a village within seven days;
of a city, a region, and kings [respectively] from a season, a half-year, and a year.
All [creatures] that eat the flesh of their own kind cause famine—
except serpents, mice, cats, and thick-furred [animals].
Those going to mate with other species cause the destruction of the region—
except for the coupling of prostitutes' [creatures?] and different-caste animals.
Imprisonment, assault, and death are [portended] by those approaching the feet, thighs, and head;
by [those approaching with] water, raw flesh, and food—group-seizure, robbery, and injury.

children.text: iṣṭaṃ vā gorasānnaṃ vā bhāradvājasya darśane/
children.translated_text: At the sighting of a lark (<s>bhāradvāja</s>), desired [food] or food with cow-products [is obtained];
at [the sighting of] a blue jay with a full beak, great gain from the right.
The francolin (<s>kapiñjala</s>) from the left and right is best, and from the front;
the partridge (<s>tittiri</s>) is best from behind; elsewhere, both are condemned.

children.text: anulomo vṛṣo nardan dhanyo gaur mahiṣas tathā/
children.translated_text: A bull bellowing in the natural direction is auspicious; likewise the cow and the buffalo.
A donkey standing facing [the traveler's] chest [portends] obstruction of the journey.

children.text: ulūkī vāmataḥ kṣemyā dakṣiṇena ca kokilā/
children.translated_text: A female owl from the left is auspicious; the cuckoo from the right.

children.text: śarkariś ca (?) mayūraś ca śasyate dakṣiṇe sadā//
children.translated_text: The <s>śarkari</s> (a bird) and the peacock are always praised from the right.

children.text: vṛkāḥ śṛgālāḥ śārdūlā viḍālā gardabhāḥ śunaḥ/
children.translated_text: Wolves, jackals, tigers, cats, donkeys, and dogs
from the left are to be known as wealth-bringers; deer from the right.
An empty pot [approaching] in the natural direction is praised; one seeking water is favorable for one wishing to travel;
especially for those setting out for theft, knowledge, trade, or wealth.
Chapter 24: Jackal Howling (<s>śivāruta</s>)
A <s>śivā</s> (jackal) from behind, when honored [i.e., auspicious], is calm, free from meat and bones;
one with a cruel sound and excessively blazing is honored in cruel undertakings.

children.text: pūrvodīcyoḥ śivā śastā śāntā sarvatra pūjitā/
children.translated_text: A <s>śivā</s> in the east or north is praised; a calm one is honored everywhere.
A smoky one facing [the traveler] kills; one blazing in voice [kills] the lords of the directions.

children.text: [rājā kumāro netā ca dūtaḥ śreṣṭhī caro dvijaḥ/
children.translated_text: [A king, a prince, a commander, an envoy, a chief merchant, a spy, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,
and an elephant-keeper—these are from the east onward; <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and others in the four directions.]
Blazing in all directions is inauspicious; especially inauspicious by day.

children.text: pure sainye 'pasavyā ca kaṣṭā pūrvonmukhā śivā//
children.translated_text: In a city or army, from the left, a <s>śivā</s> facing east is dreadful.

children.text: yāhīty agnibhayaṃ śāsti ṭāṭeti mṛticoditā\footnote{Bṣ 89.6b mṛtavedikā}/
children.translated_text: "Go!" announces danger from fire; "<s>ṭāṭa</s>" is proclaimed as death.
"Alas, alas, evil deed!" it declares; with flames, it destroys the region.

children.text: naiva dāruṇatām eke svajvālāyāḥ\footnote{Bṣ 89.7b sajvālāyāḥ} pracakṣate/
children.translated_text: Some do not ascribe fearfulness to one with its own flame [i.e., natural saliva];

children.text: arkādyanalavat tasyā vaktrāj jvālā svabhāvataḥ\footnote{Bṣ 89.7d vaktraṃ lālāsvabhāvataḥ}//
children.translated_text: for the flame from its mouth is by nature, like the Sun's fire.
One that echoes another [jackal] from the south—that one announces imprisonment, slaughter, and death.

children.text: vāruṇyābhirutā\footnote{Bṣ 89.8c anurutā} saiva saṃsate salile mṛtim//
children.translated_text: Accompanied by [a cry] from the western direction, the same [bird] foretells death in water.
Undisturbed hearing — the desired [result]; gain of wealth; arrival of a beloved;

children.text: kṣobhāt pradhānabhedaś ca vāhanānām asampadaḥ\footnote{Bṣ 89.9d ca sampadaḥ}/
children.translated_text: From disturbance — splitting among the chiefs and misfortune for vehicles.

children.text: phalam ā saptamād etad agrāhyaṃ parato rute/
children.translated_text: This result [applies] up to the seventh [call]; beyond that, the cry should not be taken [as significant].

children.text: yāmyāyāṃ tadviparyastaṃ phalaṃ ṣaṭpañcamād rute\footnote{Bṣ 89.10d ṛte}//
children.translated_text: In the southern [direction], the result is reversed, except for the fifth and sixth [calls].

children.text: yā romāṃcaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ śakṛnmūtraṃ ca vājinām/
children.translated_text: A [bird-cry] that causes goosebumps in humans, excrement and urine in horses,

children.text: rāvāt trāsaṃ ca janayet sā śivā na śivapradā//
children.translated_text: And fright from its call — that <s>śivā</s> (jackal) does not give auspiciousness.
When fallen silent after a counter-cry from men, elephants, or horses,

children.text: yā śivā sā śivaṃ sainye pure vā saṃprayacchati//E11
children.translated_text: That <s>śivā</s> bestows auspiciousness upon the army or the city.
Chapter 25: <s>Vāyaseṅgita</s> (Behavior of Crows).

children.text: śasto nīḍas tu vaiśākhe padape nirupadrave/
children.translated_text: A nest is auspicious in <s>Vaiśākha</s> [month], on an unharmed tree;
Rising of the country [is indicated] by [nesting in] anthills, shrines, granaries, houses, and such.
For crows, in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> [month], two, three, or four chicks are auspicious;
Colors of red-ochre, white, or spotted [in eggs] indicate thieves, fire, or death.
Crows scattering their eggs [foretell] both famine and pestilence;
When the chicks are deformed, or when there are no chicks, the purpose is accomplished.

children.text: hared upanayed vāpi yad dravyaṃ vāyaso 'grataḥ/
children.translated_text: Whatever object a crow carries away or brings before [a person],
That should be understood as indicating loss or gain; if golden-yellow, one should declare [accordingly].

children.text: raktadravyaṃ pradagdhaṃ vā nyasan gehe 'gnidaḥ smṛtaḥ/
children.translated_text: A red object, or a burnt one, placed in a house is declared to indicate fire;
Grass, ashes, bones, or hair [placed] on a bed indicate the master's death.
When [crows are] in confusion in the sky above the city or the army, there is danger from wind;
Those circling leftward [indicate] benefit for oneself; those circling rightward [indicate] something arising from others.
When accompanied by other birds, there is dissension; when standing in a circular formation, obstruction;

children.text: vargataś cābhighātaḥ syād ripuvṛddhiś ca nirbhayaiḥ//
children.translated_text: Attack from groups [is indicated]; increase of enemies [is indicated] by fearless [crows].
When [a crow] pecks at a sandal, parasol, vehicle, limb, weapon, or shadow,

children.text: mṛtyuṃ tatsvāmino brūyāt pūjā syāt tatprapūjane//
children.translated_text: One should declare the death of that [person's] master; worship [of that person] will result from its honoring [him].
Carrying wood, rope, bones, pith-less things, hair, or thorns while crying,
It indicates danger from wild beasts, snakes, disease, weapons, fire, and thieves.
Battle [is indicated] when [crows settle] on parts of the army; theft when [they] scratch themselves;
Moving at night [indicates] destruction; [a crow] stealing grain [indicates] famine.
A crow stationed on the left side is best; also one going from right to left;
A crow is auspicious from either side when it moves in the direction of the march.
A crow level with the traveler's ear gives safety but not gain of wealth;
One going from left to right is undesirable; or [one] at the same [level] going against [the direction].

children.text: viruvan cāgrataḥ pakṣe dhūnvan dhvāṃkṣo bhayapradaḥ/
children.translated_text: A crow crying ahead, shaking its wings, causes fear;

children.text: pratyurasy upasarpan ca saṃsparśan ca tathā bhavet//
children.translated_text: One approaching toward the chest and touching [the traveler] likewise [causes fear].
A crow standing on one foot, flapping its wings, swooping and spitting,
Causes slaughter and bondage when crying while perched on a donkey or a boar.
A crow perched upon a boar whose body is smeared with mud

children.text: vāyasaḥ śasyate yātus tūṣṇībhūto ruvann api//
children.translated_text: Is auspicious for the traveler, whether silent or crying.
One perched on a milk-tree, goat, buffalo, or cow gives dairy products;
One tearing leaves gives food; one pecking at water gives drink.
Chapter 26: <s>Śveṅgita</s> (Behavior of Dogs).
A dog urinating on men, horses, sun-parasols, elephants, weapons, banners, or bodies [indicates] victory;

children.text: sabhayo vicaran vinā nimittaṃ na śubhaś cābhimukho bhaṣan likhan gām//
children.translated_text: One moving about fearfully, without any omen, is not auspicious; one barking while facing [the traveler] and scratching the ground [is inauspicious].

children.text: uccair bhaṣaṇaṃ samāgatānāṃ dīnaṃ vābhirutaṃ raviṃ nirīkṣya/
children.translated_text: Dogs barking loudly when assembled, or crying feebly while gazing at the sun,

children.text: saṃgharadanajṛmbhaṇe ca neṣṭe prasthāneṣu tathā vidhūnanaṃ ca//
children.translated_text: And group-biting, yawning are undesirable at departures; likewise shaking.

children.text: pūrṇāsyatvaṃ ghrāyakatvaṃ ca yātuḥ prādakṣiṇyaṃ maithunaṃ cānulomam/
children.translated_text: Having a full mouth, sniffing, circumambulating the traveler clockwise, and mating in the direction [of march] —

children.text: yātrākāle sārameyasya śastaṃ padbhyāṃ mūrdhanaḥ svasya kaṇḍūyanaṃ ca//E3
children.translated_text: These are auspicious for a dog at the time of an expedition; and scratching one's own head with the paws.
Chapter 27: <s>Maṅgalāmaṅgala</s> (Auspicious and Inauspicious [Objects]).
Mustard seeds, mirrors, milk, ointments, braided [hair], and after-offerings with meat, full water-pots,
Turbans, water-vessels, prominent men, half-measures, male vehicles, <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), and parasols,
Curds, honey, ghee, <s>gorocanā</s> (ox-bile pigment), maidens, banners, gold, lotuses, auspicious seats, and conch-shells,
White bulls, flowers, garments, fish, groups of brahmins, astrologers, trusted persons, and those of beautiful attire,
Blazing flames, peacock[-feathers], fruits, unbroken rice, sugarcane, and eatables, elephants, drums, goads, <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks), and weapons,
And varieties of gems headed by emerald, ruby, <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby), crystal, and <s>maṇi</s> (jewels) —

children.text: svayam atha racitāny ayatnato vā yadi kathitāni bhavanti maṅgalāni/
children.translated_text: If these auspicious [objects] are arranged by oneself, or happen to appear effortlessly,

children.text: sa jayati sakalāṃ tato dharitrīṃ grahaṇadṛgālabhanaśrutair upāsya//
children.translated_text: He conquers the entire earth thereby, worshipping them by grasping, looking at, touching, and hearing [them].
Cotton, herbs, black grain, salt, eunuchs, bones, sesame oil, fat,
Mud, charcoal, molasses, snake-skins, dung — these cause distress, [as do] the diseased;
The wind-afflicted, the mad, the stupid, firewood, grass, chaff, the hungry, the emaciated, buttermilk, and enemies,
The shaven-headed, the anointed, those with loose hair, the fallen, and those in <s>kāṣāya</s> (ochre) robes are inauspicious.
One should proceed along a road resounding with vigorous drums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, conches, and kettledrums, with banners and archway-tops,
With abundant flowers, sprinkled water, settled dust, fragrant [atmosphere], and well-dressed people.
Chapter 28: <s>Dhvajātapatrādiśakuna</s> (Omens from Banners, Parasols, etc.).
If the banner, parasol, or weapon of men falls to the ground during a march,

children.text: uttiṣṭhato vāmbaram eti saṅgaṃ patec ca vā tannṛpateḥ kṣayāya/
children.translated_text: Or if while being raised it goes to the sky and meets [with obstruction], or if it falls — that [indicates] the king's destruction.
Should ringworm, cold, eczema, ear or eye disease, or boils arise

children.text: prāyo bale netari vā nṛpe vā jānīta rājño bhayakāraṇaṃ tat//
children.translated_text: Mostly in the army, or in the commander, or in the king — know that to be a cause of danger for the king.
Lying supine, sitting, passing wind, spitting, seeing bad [sights], and coughing
