children.text: neṣṭāni śabdāś ca tathaiva yātur āgacchatiṣṭhapraviśasthirādyāḥ//
children.translated_text: Are undesirable; and likewise words [such as] 'come,' 'stay,' 'enter,' 'stop,' and such — for the traveler.

children.text: kāryam tu mūlaśakune 'nyataraje tadahni vidyāt phalaṃ niyatam evam ime vicintyāḥ/
children.translated_text: But in the fundamental omen, or in one arising from another, the result on that day should be known as certain; thus these should be considered;

children.text: prārambhayānasamaye tu tathā praveśe grāhyaṃ kṣutam na śubhadaṃ kvacid apy uśanti//
children.translated_text: At the time of beginning the journey and at the time of entering [the vehicle], sneezing is to be accepted — they say it is never auspicious anywhere.

children.text: krośād ūrdhvaṃ śakunavirutaṃ niṣphalaṃ prāhur eke
children.translated_text: Some say that the cry of an omen-bird beyond one <s>krośa</s> (about 2 miles) is without result;

children.text: tatrāniṣṭe prathamaśukune mānayet paṃca ṣaḍ vā/
children.translated_text: In the case of an inauspicious first omen, the king should perform five or six
<s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls); if the second is likewise inauspicious, sixteen;

children.text: pratyāgacchet svabhavanam ato yady aniṣṭas tṛtīyaḥ//
children.translated_text: He should return to his own dwelling if the third is inauspicious.

children.text: cakre varāhamihiraḥ śakunopadeśam uddeśato munimatāny avalokya samyak/
children.translated_text: <s>Varāhamihira</s> composed this instruction on omens in outline, having properly examined the opinions of the sages;

children.text: yad granthavistarabhayād avijānato vā noktaṃ tad anyakathitād api cintanīyam//E6
children.translated_text: What has not been stated, due to fear of the work's length or due to ignorance, should be considered from the statements of others.
Chapter 29: <s>Niveśa</s> (Encampment).

children.text: snigdhā sthirā surabhigulmalatā sugandhā śastā pradakṣiṇajalā ca nivāsabhūmiḥ/
children.translated_text: A campsite that is moist, firm, with fragrant shrubs and creepers, sweet-smelling, and with water flowing clockwise is recommended;
One with the opposite qualities, and full of hair, gravel, bones, anthills, thorns, and <s>vibhītaka</s> [trees] is undesirable.
Having reached the camp, one should engage in [recitations about] gods, the guru, brahmins, holy men, friends, pilgrimage sites, legends, victories, and auspicious stories;

children.text: hatvā paśuṃ ripugṛhākṛtam udyame ca prāsyātha vānnamayam asya vidhāya rūpam//
children.translated_text: Having slain an animal fashioned in the form of the enemy's house, and at the time of attack, one should then offer food, making it in the form of that [enemy].
For one who has camped in one place, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and <s>Cyavana</s> have said:
The expedition should be resumed after three, five, or seven days, with an auspicious [configuration].

children.text: tac cāyuktam iti prāhur horāśāstravido janāḥ/
children.translated_text: But that is said to be improper by those versed in the <s>horā</s> (horoscopic) treatise;
The expedition is concluded upon attaining the fruit of the desired purpose.
Chapter 30: <s>Abhiyojya</s> (The Enemy to Be Attacked).
One who is given to provocation, harsh-spoken, whose servants are disaffected, who pursues others' wives,
Who is greedy, without allies, addicted to vices, ungrateful, a breaker of conventions, whose kingdom is ruined by taxation,

children.text: visrambhahā krodhavaśo nṛśaṃsaḥ kṣudraḥ pramādī na bahuśrutaś ca/
children.translated_text: A betrayer of trust, subject to anger, cruel, mean, negligent, and not learned —

children.text: divyāntarikṣakṣitijair vikārair nipīḍito yaḥ sa tu daivahīnaḥ//
children.translated_text: And one who is afflicted by portents of the three kinds — celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial — he is devoid of divine [favor].
By a king of the opposite qualities, such an enemy, merely upon being attacked,

children.text: tarur ghunair jagdha ivāttavīryo mahān api kṣipram upaiti bhaṅgam//E3
children.translated_text: Like a tree eaten by termites with its strength sapped, even if great, quickly meets destruction.
Chapter 31: <s>Senāvātavṛṣṭyulkābhūgarjitasandhyā</s> (Army, Wind, Rain, Meteors, Earthquakes, Thunder, and Twilight).
An army whose distinguished warriors have been hated, deprived of the power of men, lacking in discipline, and whose best elephants are dead,

children.text: sotpātaprakṛtiviparyayānuyātā śokārtā ripuvaśam āśu yāti senā//
children.translated_text: Accompanied by portents and reversal of natural conditions, afflicted with grief — quickly comes under the enemy's control.

children.text: saṃgrāme vayam amaradvijaprasādāj jyoṣyāmo ripubalam āśv asaṃśayena/
children.translated_text: "We shall conquer the enemy's forces quickly, without doubt, by the grace of the gods and brahmins" —

children.text: yasyaivaṃ bhavati bale janapravādaḥ so 'lpo 'pi pracurabalaṃ ripuṃ nihanti//
children.translated_text: In whichever army such popular saying prevails, even a small [force] destroys an enemy of abundant strength.
A wind that throws up fine grass, dust, leaves, and birds, that breaks the tops of parasols and banners,
That is foul-smelling, that causes elephant-rut and emaciation of people, that whirls up clods and heaps [of debris] —
Such a wind gives the traveler undesirable [results]; auspicious is one that blows in the direction of the march,
Refreshing, fragrant, moving clockwise, and sweet — it gives success.
A mass of clouds that is broad, dense, moving in the direction [of march], smooth, resembling trees, mountains, cities, desirable objects, and beings —

children.text: jayadam ubhayapārśvādhiṣṭhitaṃ pṛṣṭhato vā na śubhakaram ato 'nyad yānakāle nṛbhartuḥ//
children.translated_text: Is victory-giving when stationed on both sides or behind; other than this, it is not auspicious at the time of the king's march.
Those [clouds] of despicable creatures, <s>piśāca</s>-like, variegated, resembling flesh or animal forms, and harsh,

children.text: vajramucaḥ kṣatajāśmamuco vā balabhayam āśu janāḥ kathayanti//
children.translated_text: Or those that discharge thunderbolts, or hurl blood and stones — people say they quickly [cause] danger to the army.

children.text: bhṛśaṃ kṣaranto rudhirāruṇā vā saśakracāpā khararūkṣanādāḥ/
children.translated_text: Those [clouds] streaming excessively, blood-red, accompanied by <s>Indra</s>'s bow (rainbow), with harsh, rough sounds,
Having the appearance of various forms resembling battle equipment — when seen in the sky, they [portend] battle.
Rain occurring out of season causes danger to the army within seven days;
Some praise an expedition set forth with dark rain-clouds.
When clouds are variegated, the commander of the army is slain; when clouds are yellow, there is disease;

children.text: kṣc coṣṇāyāṃ bhavati na cirād ambudāyāṃ vināśaḥ//
children.translated_text: When hot, there is drought shortly; when [truly] rain-bearing, there is destruction.
A [meteor] going leftward destroys vehicles; otherwise, [it destroys] women;
When stationary in a cage-like formation, [it destroys] the commander of the army from all sides.

children.text: cāpam aindram anulomam akhaṇḍaṃ projjvalaṃ bahulam āyatam iṣṭam/
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>'s bow (rainbow), when moving in the direction [of march], unbroken, blazing, thick, and extended, is desired;
Thunder accompanied by a shower like the pouring of a water-pot, equal to a churning ocean, [indicates] victory.

children.text: tanvī pralambā vijayāya dīrghā taḍid ghanasphūrjathuvarjitā ca/
children.translated_text: A thin, hanging, long lightning-flash [brings] victory; one free from thunder and thick clouds [is also favorable];
A thunderbolt that falls not too close is auspicious; its crash-sound occurring clockwise [indicates] attainment.

children.text: lagne 'rkendū nighnatī śasti paurān ulkā hanyād yātupaurān grahāś ca/
children.translated_text: A meteor striking the Sun or Moon in the ascendant [portends well] for citizens; a meteor destroys the traveler's citizens and [their] planets;

children.text: yātuḥ śastā sambhṛtā vā dhruvarkṣe neṣṭāto 'nyā dhūminī śyāvaraktā//
children.translated_text: For the traveler, a meteor concentrated in a fixed <s>nakṣatra</s> is auspicious; other than this, one that is smoky and dark-red is undesirable.
It would destroy the king, citizens, countrymen, servants, lotus-growers, thieves, and brahmins

children.text: velā kramaśo dināditaḥ kāṣṭhāyāṃ ca sa yatra bhūsvanaś ca//
children.translated_text: In order of the time-periods starting from the beginning of the day; and [it affects] the direction in which the earth-sound [occurs].

children.text: śastā śāntadvijamṛgaghuṣṭā sandhyā snigdhā mṛduṣavanā ca/
children.translated_text: An evening twilight that is peaceful, with [sounds of] brahmins and animals, smooth, gentle, and agreeable is auspicious;

children.text: pāṃśudhvastā janapadanāśaṃ dhatte rūkṣā rudhiranibhā vā//E13
children.translated_text: One that is dusty causes destruction of the country; one that is harsh or blood-colored [likewise].
Chapter 32: <s>Utpāta</s> (Portents).
A halo around the Sun or Moon, together with planets of the enemy's faction,
When smooth and unbroken, gives victory; when having many circles, it gives evil.
Moving counter-clockwise and excessively abundant — undesirable; clockwise is desired;

children.text: nīhāraḥ pāṃśupātaś ca hitaḥ snigdhaḥ pradakṣiṇaḥ//
children.translated_text: Mist and fall of dust, when smooth and clockwise, are beneficial.
A <s>gandharva</s>-city (mirage) destroys, beginning from the east, the king, [then]

children.text: baleśaṃ yuvarājaṃ ca purohitam iti kramāt//
children.translated_text: The army-commander, the crown prince, and the chief priest, in order.
When white and so forth, [it affects] brahmins and others; in the intermediate directions, mixed-caste [persons];

children.text: pradakṣiṇaṃ tu yātrāyāṃ jayadaṃ neṣṭam anyathā//
children.translated_text: When clockwise during an expedition, it gives victory; otherwise it is undesirable.
A burning of the quarters, when approaching clockwise, gives victory;

children.text: śvabhronnate vadho rājño jayāya vyatyayena ca//
children.translated_text: When the [ground] sinks and rises, death of the king; and the reverse [indicates] victory.

children.text: ghṛtāmbupayasāṃ srāve cyute vṛkṣāc ca tatkṣayaḥ/
children.translated_text: When ghee, water, or milk oozes, or when [something] falls from a tree, that [person's] destruction [is indicated];

children.text: taile ca nāśo mukhyānāṃ rakte śastrakṛtaṃ bhayam//
children.translated_text: When oil [oozes], destruction of the chiefs; when blood [appears], danger from weapons.

children.text: madyena tu mitho bhedo rugbhayaṃ dadhinisrave/
children.translated_text: When liquor [oozes], mutual dissension; when curds stream, danger from disease;
When flowers arise from [other] flowers, one should predict the approach of an enemy army.
Excessive drying up of much water, or a well overflowing with blood —
These would cause the death of the king within half a year; when the stream diminishes, the approach of the enemy.
When there is rain, lightning, and thunder in a cloudless [sky], when mobile and immobile things are reversed,

children.text: dinolkāyāṃ ca pīḍyante janā bhūpatibhiḥ saha//
children.translated_text: And when there is a daytime meteor — people are afflicted, together with the king.

children.text: saptāhaṃ santatāny ato vṛṣṭir hanyān narādhipam/
children.translated_text: Continuous [portents] for seven days, followed by rain, destroy the king;

children.text: anagnijvalane puṃsāṃ vyādhir āśv eva jāyate//
children.translated_text: When there is fire [blazing] without fuel in men, disease quickly arises.
Affliction of the kingdom within six months [comes] when heat and cold are reversed;
The end of the king [comes] in the eighth month when domestic and wild animals cry out.
When creatures of city and forest frequent the forest and city [respectively],
Affliction of the kingdom in excess of a year, and destruction of the chief people.
When pillars, stones, granaries, images, platforms, or beds shift [of their own accord],

children.text: gadane cāpi deśasya nāśaṃ māsatrayād vadet//
children.translated_text: And in the case of mist, one should predict the destruction of the land within three months.
The slaughter of cows, serpents, or horses [portends ruin] within half a year; a reversal [of these omens] causes the king's death.
Likewise the destruction of the land and of women, when birds, serpents, and beasts [appear unnaturally].
In rains of grain, juice, liquor, food, fruits, flowers, oil, meat, and garments,
and of sand, dust, liquid, stones mixed with gravel, and embers —
[the results are respectively:] [trouble for] the son, the wife, minor kings, the king, the land, the army, and death and suffering;
dissension, calamity, then death of the minister, disease, destruction, and the king's anger.

children.text: niśi suracāpaṃ sitavarṇādyaṃ janayati pīḍāṃ dvijapūrvāṇām/
children.translated_text: A rainbow at night, beginning with a white color, causes affliction to those headed by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>;

children.text: bhavati ca yasyāṃ diśi taddiśyaṃ narapatimukhyaṃ na cirād dhanyāt//
children.translated_text: and in whichever direction it appears, it would soon slay the foremost king of that direction.
Sounds in the sky of deer, cattle, donkeys, goats, and elephants are soon portents of danger.

children.text: vibudhapatidhvajatoraṇapātaḥ phalam idam eva karoti nṛpāṇām//E18
children.translated_text: The falling of <s>Indra</s>'s banner or a triumphal arch — this very result befalls kings.
Chapter 33: The Capture of a City or Fort.
When benefic [planets] are in the twelfth, <s>kendra</s> (angular), and eighth houses, and malefics are in the third, sixth, and eleventh houses,
with the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant) in a <s>kendra</s>, or when <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) or the preceptor of the <s>Daityas</s> (Venus) [is so placed],

children.text: sarvārambhaphalaprasiddhir udaye rāśau ca kartuḥ śubhe
children.translated_text: the success of the fruit of all undertakings [is assured]. When the rising sign belongs to the doer and is auspicious,
with a fixed or own sign rising, [that is the time] for construction of a house or entering one.

children.text: krūrodaye tadahani vyatipātayoge rikte tithāv ṛtusamāptiṣu vaidhṛte vā/
children.translated_text: On a day when a cruel [planet] is rising, in the <s>Vyatīpāta</s> yoga, on a <s>rikta</s> (empty) <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), at the conclusion of a season, or in <s>Vaidhṛti</s>,

children.text: tīkṣṇograbheṣu ca hutāśaviṣābhighātaraudrāṇi siddhim upayāny asite ca pakṣe//
children.translated_text: and in fierce and terrible [<s>nakṣatras</s>] — acts of fire, poison, assault, and destruction achieve success; also in the dark fortnight.
From whichever direction <s>Ketu</s>, a meteor, a son of the Sun (Saturn), <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Kīlaka</s>, or <s>Kuja</s> (Mars) has entered the disk [of the Sun or Moon],

children.text: sūryendvoḥ pariveṣakhaṇḍam athavā dṛśyeta yasyāṃ diśi/
children.translated_text: or in whichever direction a halo or partial halo of the Sun or Moon is seen,
and from whichever direction jackals, dogs, serpents, ants, hares, deer, crows, and the like enter the city

children.text: sainye vāpi yato viśanti hi tataḥ śastroḥ puraṃ ghātayet//
children.translated_text: or the army — from that direction the enemy should attack and destroy the city.

children.text: pātālarkṣe rāhuketvoḥ pure 'res toyocchittiḥ sālapātaś ca kāryaḥ/
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāhu</s> or <s>Ketu</s> are in the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Pātāla</s> (the nadir), one should cut off the water supply and fell the <s>śāla</s> trees of the enemy's city.

children.text: jāmitrasthe bhūmije 'syāṃśake vā putreṇendor vīkṣite 'gniḥ pradeyaḥ//E5
children.translated_text: When Mars is in the seventh house or its division, or when the Moon's fifth [house] is aspected [by Mars], fire should be applied.
Chapter 34: Post-Victory [Conduct].
By burning of the directions, [showers of] blood, dust, heat, and rain, by earthquakes and thunderbolts, and by unnatural phenomena,

children.text: yuddhānte mṛgaśakunaiś ca dīptanādair no bhadraṃ bhavati jaye 'pi pārthivasya//
children.translated_text: and by animals and birds uttering fierce cries at the end of battle — even in victory, no good befalls the king.
When animals and birds are auspicious, the breeze is gentle and pleasant,
the planets have bright rays, and the circle of directions is free of dust,

children.text: yadānyad api vaikṛtaṃ na vijayāvasāne bhavet
children.translated_text: and when no other unnatural phenomenon occurs at the conclusion of victory,

children.text: tadā sukham akaṇṭakaṃ nṛpatir atti deśaṃ ripoḥ/
children.translated_text: then the king enjoys the enemy's land in comfort, free from thorns.

children.text: udvāham akālotsavam abhiṣekaṃ cātmajasya yaḥ kṛtvā/
children.translated_text: He who performs a marriage, an untimely festival, or the consecration of his son,
and is not hindered in his departure — he proceeds on festival days.
Upon obtaining the enemy's territory and city, the king should not harass the property of virtuous people, gods, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
nor the women of noble families.
He should not kill those who have lost their elephants, horses, and weapons, nor those who are afflicted, frightened,
and on an auspicious <s>tithi</s>, day, and <s>nakṣatra</s>, with a cheerful army, he should enter [the conquered city].
Having returned to his own territory, the lord among honored kings should offer the tribute and additional offerings that had been promised
to the <s>pramathas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, spirits, and deities of the first rank, according to the rite previously described.

children.text: iti manujapatir yathopadeśaṃ bhagaṇavidāṃ prakaroti yo vacāṃsi/
children.translated_text: Thus the lord of men who acts according to the instructions of those skilled in the movements of the celestial bodies,
swiftly attains sovereignty over the entire circle of kings, like <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) in heaven.
